subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
examTitle: ICAI CA Final Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics (AAAPE) — Full 100-Question Comprehensive Examination
coverage: All 11 Syllabus Modules of ICAI CA Final AAAPE (Standards on Auditing, Entities, Reporting, Assurance, Forensic, Digital, Governance & Ethics)

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 240 - Management Override of Controls & Journal Entries
questions.question: During the audit of Zenith Steel Ltd., the engagement team notices that the CFO posted several manual journal entries directly to revenue and inventory accounts at 11:45 PM on March 31 without any supporting narration or supervisory approval. Under SA 240 'The Auditor's Responsibilities Relating to Fraud in an Audit of Financial Statements', which specific audit procedure is mandatory to address the risk of management override of controls?
options: Test the appropriateness of journal entries recorded in the general ledger and other adjustments made in the preparation of the financial statements, review accounting estimates for biases, and evaluate the business rationale for significant unusual transactions.
Rely entirely on the written representation letter obtained from the Chief Executive Officer and CFO confirming that all journal entries are legitimate.
Immediately resign from the audit engagement without performing any testing because manual journal entries automatically signify criminal fraud.
Qualify the audit opinion without examining the entries because internal financial controls are deemed to have completely failed.
questions.ref: SA 240, Paragraph 32 - Management Override of Controls
questions.explanation: Under SA 240.32, to address the risk of management override of controls, the auditor is mandatorily required to: (1) Test the appropriateness of journal entries recorded in the general ledger and other adjustments made in the preparation of the financial statements; (2) Review accounting estimates for biases and evaluate whether circumstances producing bias represent risk of material misstatement due to fraud; and (3) Evaluate the business rationale for significant transactions that are outside the normal course of business.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 505 - External Confirmations & Management Refusal
questions.question: In the statutory audit of Omega Pharma Ltd., trade receivables constitute 35% of total assets. The auditor selects 25 high-value debtors for external confirmation under SA 505. Management requests the auditor not to send confirmation requests to 4 major debtors representing 18% of total receivables, citing sensitive commercial renegotiations. What is the auditor's required course of action under SA 505?
options: Inquire into management's reasons for refusal, seek audit evidence regarding validity and reasonableness, evaluate the implications on risk assessment, and perform alternative audit procedures. If refusal is unreasonable and alternative evidence cannot be obtained, communicate with TCWG and modify the opinion.
Accept management's refusal unconditionally as commercial negotiations take precedence over auditing standards.
Automatically issue an adverse opinion without seeking any explanation or performing alternative procedures.
Issue a clean unmodified opinion provided management issues a post-dated cheque for the unconfirmed balances.
questions.ref: SA 505, Paragraphs 8 & 9 - Management's Refusal to Allow the Auditor to Send a Confirmation Request
questions.explanation: Under SA 505.8-9, if management refuses to allow confirmation requests, the auditor must: (a) Inquire as to management's reasons and seek audit evidence as to their validity and reasonableness; (b) Evaluate implications on assessment of relevant risks of material misstatement, including fraud risk; and (c) Perform alternative audit procedures. If the auditor concludes that refusal is unreasonable or is unable to obtain relevant and reliable audit evidence from alternative procedures, the auditor shall communicate with TCWG and determine the implication for the audit and the opinion under SA 705.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 570 (Revised) - Going Concern & Material Uncertainty
questions.question: Kaveri Textiles Ltd. has incurred continuous operating losses for 3 years, its net worth is negative, and working capital is severely negative. However, management has entered into a non-binding Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with a strategic investor to infuse ₹120 Crores equity subject to regulatory approvals. Management has adequately disclosed the existence of material uncertainty in Note 28 of the financial statements and prepared the statements on a going concern basis. What is the appropriate audit reporting under SA 570 (Revised)?
options: Express an unmodified opinion and include a separate section under the heading 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern' drawing attention to Note 28.
Issue an Adverse Opinion because any company with negative net worth cannot prepare accounts on a going concern basis.
Express a Qualified Opinion citing that the MoU is non-binding and regulatory approval is uncertain.
Include the matter strictly as a Key Audit Matter (KAM) under SA 701 and omit the 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern' section.
questions.ref: SA 570 (Revised), Paragraphs 22 & 23 - Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern Adequately Disclosed
questions.explanation: Under SA 570 (Revised).22, if adequate disclosure about the material uncertainty is made in the financial statements, the auditor shall express an unmodified opinion and the auditor's report shall include a separate section under the heading 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern' to: (a) Draw attention to the note in the financial statements disclosing the matter; and (b) State that these events or conditions indicate a material uncertainty exists that may cast significant doubt on the entity's ability to continue as a going concern and that the auditor's opinion is not modified in respect of the matter.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 299 - Joint Audit Responsibilities & Disagreement
questions.question: CA Raman and CA Suresh are appointed as joint auditors of Bharat Heavy Engineering Ltd. Work is formally allocated between them: Raman is assigned procurement, inventory, and production, while Suresh is assigned sales, treasury, and statutory liabilities. During the audit, Suresh identifies serious discrepancies in treasury investments which Raman believes are immaterial. Suresh insists on modifying the audit report, while Raman wishes to issue an unmodified report. Under SA 299 'Joint Audit of Financial Statements', how should the auditors proceed?
options: The joint auditors are not required to adopt the opinion of the majority. Each joint auditor shall express their own opinion through separate audit reports, cross-referencing the report issued by the other joint auditor.
The opinion of the senior-most auditor (in age or seniority of membership) shall prevail and bind the other auditor.
They must refer the dispute to the Central Council of ICAI and withhold the audit report until ICAI issues a binding ruling.
Raman must sign the report because treasury was allocated to Suresh, so Raman has no right to dissent.
questions.ref: SA 299 (Revised), Paragraph 11 - Disagreement Among Joint Auditors
questions.explanation: Under SA 299 (Revised).11, where the joint auditors are in disagreement with regard to any matters or the opinion to be expressed, they are not bound by the view of the majority. Each joint auditor shall express his own opinion through a separate audit report. A joint auditor is not bound to adopt the majority view and shall issue a separate report, referencing the report issued by the other joint auditor(s).

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 550 - Related Parties & Arm's Length Assertion
questions.question: During the audit of Alpha Motors Ltd., the auditor discovers that the company sold commercial vehicles worth ₹45 Crores to an entity controlled by the Managing Director's brother. Management asserts in the notes that the transaction was conducted on terms equivalent to those prevailing in an arm's length transaction. Under SA 550 'Related Parties', what is the auditor's responsibility regarding this management assertion?
options: The auditor must obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence to substantiate management's assertion that the transaction was at arm's length. If management cannot support the claim and refuses to remove it, the auditor must modify the audit opinion.
The auditor has no obligation to verify arm's length claims as pricing decisions are purely executive managerial prerogatives.
The auditor can accept the assertion based solely on a written representation letter without corroborative evidence.
The auditor must refer the transaction to the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for statutory investigation.
questions.ref: SA 550, Paragraph 24 - Assertions That Related Party Transactions Were Conducted on Arm's Length Terms
questions.explanation: Under SA 550.24, if management makes an assertion in the financial statements that a related party transaction was conducted on terms equivalent to those prevailing in an arm's length transaction, the auditor shall obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence about the assertion. If the auditor is unable to obtain sufficient evidence to support this assertion, the auditor shall request management to modify the disclosure, and if management refuses, modify the opinion under SA 705.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 560 - Subsequent Events & Amended Financial Statements
questions.question: The audit report of Delta Infra Ltd. for FY 2023-24 was signed on May 15, 2024. On June 10, 2024 (before the financial statements were issued to shareholders), a catastrophic fire destroyed Delta's primary manufacturing facility with an uninsured loss of ₹80 Crores. Management amends the financial statements. The auditor agrees to extend subsequent events procedures to the date of the new audit report. What options does the auditor have regarding the audit report date under SA 560?
options: The auditor can either amend the audit report to include an additional date restricted to that amendment (dual dating) or provide a new or amended audit report with a new date extended to June 10, 2024.
The auditor must retain the original date of May 15, 2024 without mentioning the fire anywhere.
The auditor must resign immediately because the financial statements cannot be altered after signing.
The auditor can only report the matter in CARO 2020 for the subsequent financial year.
questions.ref: SA 560, Paragraphs 11 & 12 - Subsequent Events Occurring Before Issuance of Financial Statements
questions.explanation: Under SA 560.11-12, when management amends the financial statements after the audit report date but before issuance, the auditor shall extend audit procedures to the date of the new report. The auditor can either: (a) Amend the audit report to include an additional date restricted to that amendment (dual dating); or (b) Provide a new or amended auditor's report with a new date, covering all subsequent events up to the new date.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 540 (Revised) - Auditing Accounting Estimates & Fair Value
questions.question: In auditing the expected credit loss (ECL) model under Ind AS 109 of a scheduled commercial bank, the auditor evaluates management's macro-economic forward-looking point estimates. Under SA 540 (Revised) 'Auditing Accounting Estimates and Related Disclosures', which of the following is considered an auditor's independent response when estimation uncertainty is high?
options: Develop an independent point estimate or range to evaluate management's point estimate, and test the operating effectiveness of controls over how management developed the estimate.
Blindly adopt management's internal mathematical model without testing any assumptions.
Request the Reserve Bank of India to audit the ECL model on the auditor's behalf.
Disclaim the opinion automatically because estimation uncertainty is inherently subjective.
questions.ref: SA 540 (Revised), Paragraph 18 - Auditor's Further Substantive Procedures on Accounting Estimates
questions.explanation: Under SA 540 (Revised).18, in responding to the assessed risks of material misstatement for accounting estimates, the auditor's procedures shall include one or more of: (a) Testing how management made the accounting estimate; (b) Testing the operating effectiveness of controls; (c) Developing an auditor's point estimate or range; and (d) Obtaining audit evidence from events occurring up to the date of the auditor's report.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 510 - Initial Audit Engagements & Opening Balances
questions.question: CA Tarun is appointed as statutory auditor of Apex Ltd. for FY 2023-24. The prior year financial statements were audited by another auditor who expressed an unmodified opinion. Under SA 510 'Initial Audit Engagements - Opening Balances', what is Tarun's responsibility regarding opening balances?
options: Read the most recent financial statements and predecessor auditor's report, and obtain sufficient appropriate evidence about whether opening balances contain misstatements that materially affect the current period's financial statements.
Re-audit all prior period transactions from inception of the company.
Rely entirely on the predecessor auditor's report without performing any inquiry or procedures.
Disclaim an opinion on opening balances in the auditor's report for the current year.
questions.ref: SA 510, Paragraph 6 - Audit Procedures Regarding Opening Balances
questions.explanation: Under SA 510.6, the auditor shall obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence about whether the opening balances contain misstatements that materially affect the current period's financial statements by: (a) Determining whether the prior period's closing balances have been correctly brought forward; (b) Determining whether the opening balances reflect the application of appropriate accounting policies; and (c) Reviewing the predecessor auditor's working papers or evaluating current period audit procedures.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 501 - Physical Inventory Counting
questions.question: Zenith Retail Ltd. holds physical inventory worth ₹250 Crores across 12 centralized warehouses. Physical verification was conducted by management on March 31, 2024. Due to unforeseen regional lockdowns, the statutory auditor was unable to attend the physical count on that date. What does SA 501 require the auditor to do?
options: Perform physical count observation on an alternative date, and perform audit procedures on intervening transactions to assess whether changes in inventory between the count date and financial statement date are properly recorded.
Issue an immediate disclaimer of opinion without attempting alternative dates or procedures.
Accept management's internal stock register extracts as conclusive evidence.
Instruct management to cancel the financial statements and re-conduct the count after 6 months.
questions.ref: SA 501, Paragraph 5 - Attendance at Physical Inventory Counting on an Alternative Date
questions.explanation: Under SA 501.5, if physical inventory counting is conducted at a date other than the date of the financial statements, or if the auditor is unable to attend due to unforeseen circumstances, the auditor shall perform audit procedures on an alternative date and perform audit procedures on intervening transactions to reconcile changes between count date and balance sheet date.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 315 (Revised) - Five Components of Internal Control
questions.question: In identifying and assessing the risks of material misstatement under SA 315 (Revised), the auditor must obtain an understanding of the entity's internal control system. Which of the following correctly lists the five interrelated components of internal control recognized by SA 315?
options: Control Environment, Entity's Risk Assessment Process, Entity's Process to Monitor the System of Internal Control, Information System and Communication, and Control Activities.
Board Approval, External Legal Opinions, Tax Planning, Statutory Filings, and Shareholder Relations.
Budgeting, Payroll Processing, Fixed Asset Register, Cash Safeguarding, and Vendor Onboarding.
Preventive Controls, Detective Controls, Corrective Controls, Compensating Controls, and Directive Controls.
questions.ref: SA 315 (Revised), Paragraphs 21-27 - Components of System of Internal Control
questions.explanation: Under SA 315 (Revised), the auditor obtains an understanding of the entity's system of internal control across five components: (1) Control Environment; (2) Entity's Risk Assessment Process; (3) Entity's Process to Monitor the System of Internal Control; (4) Information System and Communication; and (5) Control Activities.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 320 - Materiality & Performance Materiality
questions.question: For the audit of Apex Consumer Goods Ltd. (Turnover ₹1,200 Crores, Profit Before Tax ₹60 Crores), the auditor determines Financial Statement Materiality at ₹3 Crores (5% of PBT). To reduce the probability that aggregate uncorrected and undetected misstatements exceed materiality, the auditor sets Performance Materiality at ₹2.1 Crores (70% of materiality). What is the conceptual distinction between Materiality and Performance Materiality under SA 320?
options: Materiality is determined for the financial statements as a whole based on user needs, whereas Performance Materiality is set by the auditor at a lower amount to provide a safety margin against aggregation risk during audit testing.
Performance Materiality is only used for tax computation, while Materiality is used for legal disputes.
Performance Materiality must always be exactly equal to double the overall materiality.
Materiality is set by management in the Board meeting, whereas Performance Materiality is set by ICAI.
questions.ref: SA 320, Paragraphs 9 & 11 - Performance Materiality and Materiality for the Financial Statements as a Whole
questions.explanation: Under SA 320.9 & 11, Performance Materiality means the amount or amounts set by the auditor at less than materiality for the financial statements as a whole to reduce to an appropriately low level the probability that the aggregate of uncorrected and undetected misstatements exceeds materiality for the financial statements as a whole.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Section 143(3)(i) - Internal Financial Controls Over Financial Reporting (IFC-FR)
questions.question: Under Section 143(3)(i) of the Companies Act, 2013, the auditor's report must state whether the company has adequate internal financial controls with reference to financial statements (IFC-FR) and the operating effectiveness of such controls. Which class of private companies is EXEMPT from this requirement under MCA Notification dated June 13, 2017?
options: A private company which is a one person company (OPC) or small company, or a private company having turnover less than ₹50 Crores as per latest audited financial statement AND aggregate borrowings from banks/FIs/bodies corporate less than ₹25 Crores at any time during the financial year.
All private companies are unconditionally exempt regardless of turnover or borrowing levels.
Only private companies with turnover exceeding ₹500 Crores are exempt.
No company in India is exempt from Section 143(3)(i).
questions.ref: MCA Notification G.S.R. 583(E) dated 13th June 2017 - Exemption to Private Companies u/s 143(3)(i)
questions.explanation: Under MCA Notification dated 13th June 2017, the reporting requirement on IFC-FR under Section 143(3)(i) shall not apply to a private company which: (a) Is a one person company (OPC) or a small company; OR (b) Has turnover less than ₹50 Crores as per latest audited financial statements AND aggregate borrowings from banks or financial institutions or any body corporate less than ₹25 Crores at any point of time during the financial year.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 330 - The Auditor's Responses to Assessed Risks
questions.question: Under SA 330 'The Auditor's Responses to Assessed Risks', when the auditor's assessment of risks of material misstatement at the assertion level includes an expectation that internal controls are operating effectively, what is the auditor REQUIRED to do?
options: Design and perform tests of controls to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence about the operating effectiveness of relevant controls.
Rely on management's verbal reassurance and eliminate all substantive testing.
Eliminate tests of controls and perform 100% substantive vouchers audit.
Issue a clean report without testing controls or transactions.
questions.ref: SA 330, Paragraph 8 - Tests of Controls Requirement
questions.explanation: Under SA 330.8, the auditor shall design and perform tests of controls to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence as to the operating effectiveness of relevant controls if: (a) The auditor's assessment of risks of material misstatement at the assertion level includes an expectation that the controls are operating effectively; or (b) Substantive procedures alone cannot provide sufficient appropriate audit evidence at the assertion level.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 402 - Audit Considerations Relating to Service Organizations
questions.question: Pinnacle Mutual Fund outsources its registrar and transfer agency (RTA) operations, unit capital accounting, and NAV calculations to CAMS Ltd. Under SA 402, Pinnacle's statutory auditor wants to obtain audit evidence regarding internal controls at CAMS. Which type of independent assurance report provided by CAMS's service auditor provides evidence regarding both the suitability of design AND the operating effectiveness of controls?
options: Type 2 report (Report on the description, design, and operating effectiveness of controls at a service organization throughout a specified period).
Type 1 report (Report on description and design of controls as at a specific date only).
A general character certificate issued by the local chamber of commerce.
A limited review report under SRE 2410.
questions.ref: SA 402, Paragraph 8 & SAE 3402 - Type 1 vs Type 2 Service Auditor Reports
questions.explanation: Under SA 402.8 and SAE 3402, a Type 2 report comprises a report by the service auditor on the description, design, AND operating effectiveness of controls at the service organization throughout a specified period. A Type 1 report only covers description and design suitability as at a specified date, without testing operating effectiveness.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 450 - Evaluation of Misstatements Identified During Audit
questions.question: During the audit of a construction company, the auditor discovers uncorrected misstatements totaling ₹4.2 Crores. Overall materiality is ₹5 Crores. Management refuses to adjust the errors arguing they are below materiality. Under SA 450, how should the auditor evaluate these uncorrected misstatements before forming an opinion?
options: Reassess materiality, determine whether uncorrected misstatements are material individually or in aggregate (considering their size and nature, and the particular circumstances of their occurrence), and request written representations from management regarding their immateriality.
Conclude automatically that since ₹4.2 Cr is below ₹5 Cr, no further evaluation or inquiry is required.
Force management to increase revenue by ₹4.2 Crores to balance the error.
Resign immediately without communicating with the Audit Committee.
questions.ref: SA 450, Paragraphs 10, 11 & 14 - Evaluating the Effect of Uncorrected Misstatements
questions.explanation: Under SA 450.10-14, the auditor shall determine whether uncorrected misstatements are material, individually or in aggregate. In making this determination, the auditor shall consider: (a) The size and nature of the misstatements, both in relation to particular classes of transactions and financial statements as a whole; and (b) The effect of uncorrected misstatements related to prior periods. The auditor must also request written representations from management and TCWG whether they believe the effects of uncorrected misstatements are immaterial.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 300 - Overall Audit Strategy vs Audit Plan
questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Overall Audit Strategy from the Detailed Audit Plan under SA 300 'Planning an Audit of Financial Statements'?
options: The audit strategy sets the scope, timing, and direction of the audit and guides the development of the audit plan; the audit plan is more detailed and includes the nature, timing, and extent of risk assessment procedures, further audit procedures at assertion level, and other planned audit procedures.
The audit plan is prepared first by the client, and the audit strategy is developed later by the auditor.
The audit strategy is legally binding on shareholders, while the audit plan can never be updated once written.
There is no distinction between audit strategy and audit plan; they are identical documents.
questions.ref: SA 300, Paragraphs 7, 8 & 9 - Audit Strategy and Audit Plan
questions.explanation: Under SA 300.7-9, the auditor shall establish an overall audit strategy that sets the scope, timing, and direction of the audit, and that guides the development of the audit plan. The audit plan is more detailed than the overall audit strategy in that it includes the nature, timing, and extent of audit procedures to be performed by engagement team members (risk assessment procedures and further audit procedures at assertion level).

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 315 - Significant Risks Identification
questions.question: Under SA 315 (Revised), what is defined as a 'Significant Risk' and what mandatory audit response is required under SA 330?
options: An identified risk of material misstatement for which the assessment of inherent risk is close to the upper end of the spectrum of inherent risk; for significant risks, the auditor cannot rely on controls tested in prior years and must perform substantive procedures that are specifically responsive to that risk (including tests of details).
Any risk where the value involved is greater than ₹1 Lakh.
A risk that only arises during foreign currency conversions.
A risk where management refuses to sign the balance sheet.
questions.ref: SA 315 (Revised), Paragraph 12(l) & SA 330, Paragraphs 15 & 21 - Significant Risks Definition & Audit Response
questions.explanation: Under SA 315.12(l), a significant risk is an identified risk of material misstatement for which the assessment of inherent risk is close to the upper end of the spectrum. Under SA 330.15 & 21, when the auditor plans to rely on controls over a significant risk, the auditor shall test those controls in the current period (no multi-year reliance) and shall perform substantive procedures that are specifically responsive to that risk (which must include tests of details if only substantive procedures are applied).

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Internal Control - Segregation of Duties (SoD) Conflict
questions.question: In review of the revenue cycle of Nova Logistics Ltd., the auditor observes that the senior accountant has access rights in SAP ERP to create new customer accounts, generate sales orders, approve credit limits, record journal entries, and issue credit notes. Which core internal control concept is severely compromised here?
options: Segregation of Duties (SoD) — custody of assets, authorization of transactions, execution, and recording should be separated among different individuals to prevent and detect errors or fraud in the normal course of duties.
Principle of double-entry bookkeeping.
Prudence and conservatism principle under Ind AS 1.
Going concern assumption.
questions.ref: ICAI Guidance Note on Internal Financial Controls Over Financial Reporting - Segregation of Duties
questions.explanation: Segregation of Duties (SoD) is a fundamental internal control concept where no single individual should be in a position to perpetrate and conceal errors or fraud in the normal course of their duties. Combining authorization (credit approval), recording (sales ledger & journal entries), and execution (issuing credit notes) creates a critical SoD conflict.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Audit of Specific Entities: Banks, Insurance Companies, and Government Bodies
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Bank Audit - NPA Classification Norms (90-Day Overdue)
questions.question: In the statutory branch audit of a Scheduled Commercial Bank as of March 31, 2024, a cash credit account of M/s Pragati Agro Ltd. shows an outstanding balance of ₹4.80 Crores against a sanctioned limit of ₹4.50 Crores. During the quarter ended March 31, 2024, total credits in the account were ₹12 Lakhs, whereas interest debited was ₹16 Lakhs. The account has remained continuously in excess of the sanctioned limit for 95 days. What is the asset classification of this account under RBI Prudential Norms?
options: Non-Performing Asset (NPA) — classified as Substandard Asset because the account is 'out of order' (outstanding balance remained continuously in excess of sanctioned limit for more than 90 days and credits were insufficient to cover interest debited).
Standard Asset, because total turnover of the borrower exceeds ₹50 Crores.
Special Mention Account - 0 (SMA-0), because overdue period is below 180 days.
Loss Asset, requiring immediate 100% write-off.
questions.ref: RBI Master Circular - Prudential Norms on Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning (IRACP)
questions.explanation: Under RBI IRACP norms, a Cash Credit/Overdraft account is treated as NPA if it is 'out of order'. An account is treated as out of order if the outstanding balance remains continuously in excess of the sanctioned limit/drawing power for 90 days, or if credits during the quarter are not enough to cover interest debited. Here, it exceeded limits for 95 days and credits (₹12L) were less than interest (₹16L); hence it must be classified as an NPA (Substandard Asset).

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Audit of Specific Entities: Banks, Insurance Companies, and Government Bodies
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Bank Audit - Provisioning Percentages for Substandard & Doubtful Assets
questions.question: A bank advance of ₹100 Lakhs was classified as Doubtful Asset - Category 2 (Doubtful for more than 1 year and up to 3 years) as on March 31, 2024. The realizable value of tangible security held is ₹60 Lakhs (verified by an approved valuer within the last 3 years). What is the mandatory RBI provisioning required for this asset?
options: Total provision ₹64 Lakhs (100% on unsecured portion ₹40L = ₹40L, plus 40% on secured portion ₹60L = ₹24L).
Total provision ₹100 Lakhs (100% on total advance).
Total provision ₹25 Lakhs (25% on total advance).
Total provision ₹40 Lakhs (only on the unsecured portion).
questions.ref: RBI Master Circular on IRACP - Provisioning Norms for Doubtful Assets (D2)
questions.explanation: For Doubtful Assets Category 2 (D2 - doubtful for >1 year and up to 3 years): (1) Unsecured portion (where realisable value of security is nil) attracts 100% provision: (100 - 60) × 100% = ₹40 Lakhs; (2) Secured portion attracts 40% provision: ₹60L × 40% = ₹24 Lakhs. Total Provision = ₹40L + ₹24L = ₹64 Lakhs.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Audit of Specific Entities: Banks, Insurance Companies, and Government Bodies
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Bank Audit - Drawing Power (DP) Calculation
questions.question: A borrower is sanctioned a working capital Cash Credit limit of ₹200 Lakhs against hypothecation of stocks and book debts. As on March 31, 2024, stock value is ₹250 Lakhs (including unpaid stock under letter of credit of ₹50 Lakhs and obsolete stock of ₹20 Lakhs). Eligible trade debtors are ₹80 Lakhs (excluding debts older than 90 days). The margin stipulated by the bank is 25% on paid stock and 40% on debtors. What is the Drawing Power (DP) for the borrower?
options: Drawing Power = ₹183 Lakhs (Paid stock ₹180L - 25% margin = ₹135L; Debtors ₹80L - 40% margin = ₹48L; Total = ₹183 Lakhs).
Drawing Power = ₹200 Lakhs (Sanctioned limit is automatically the Drawing Power).
Drawing Power = ₹247.5 Lakhs (Total stock ₹250L + Debtors ₹80L less margins).
Drawing Power = ₹150 Lakhs (Flat 75% of sanctioned limit).
questions.ref: ICAI Guidance Note on Audit of Banks - Verification of Advances & Drawing Power
questions.explanation: Eligible Stock = Gross Stock (₹250L) - Unpaid LC Stock (₹50L) - Obsolete Stock (₹20L) = ₹180 Lakhs. DP on Stock = 180 × (1 - 0.25) = ₹135 Lakhs. Eligible Debtors = ₹80 Lakhs. DP on Debtors = 80 × (1 - 0.40) = ₹48 Lakhs. Total Drawing Power = 135 + 48 = ₹183 Lakhs. (Since DP of ₹183L is less than sanctioned limit of ₹200L, the borrower can draw up to ₹183 Lakhs).

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Audit of Specific Entities: Banks, Insurance Companies, and Government Bodies
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Bank Audit - Basel III CRAR & Capital Adequacy
questions.question: Under RBI Basel III capital adequacy guidelines, what is the minimum regulatory Total Capital Adequacy Ratio (CRAR) and minimum Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio that scheduled commercial banks in India are required to maintain (excluding Capital Conservation Buffer)?
options: Minimum Total CRAR of 9.0% and minimum CET1 ratio of 5.5% of Risk-Weighted Assets (RWAs).
Minimum Total CRAR of 12.0% and minimum CET1 ratio of 8.0%.
Minimum Total CRAR of 8.0% and minimum CET1 ratio of 4.5% (Basel international norm without RBI enhancement).
Minimum Total CRAR of 15.0% for all public and private banks.
questions.ref: RBI Master Circular - Basel III Capital Regulations
questions.explanation: Under RBI Basel III regulations for commercial banks in India (which are more stringent than the Basel Committee norms): Minimum Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) is 5.5% (vs Basel III global 4.5%); Minimum Tier 1 capital is 7.0%; and Minimum Total Capital (CRAR) is 9.0% (vs Basel III global 8.0%) of Risk-Weighted Assets, plus Capital Conservation Buffer (CCB) of 2.5% in Common Equity Tier 1.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Audit of Specific Entities: Banks, Insurance Companies, and Government Bodies
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Bank Audit - Long Form Audit Report (LFAR)
questions.question: What is the purpose and structural deadline of the Long Form Audit Report (LFAR) prepared by statutory branch auditors and statutory central auditors of a bank?
options: The LFAR is a comprehensive questionnaire formulated by RBI seeking detailed comments on credit appraisal, sanctioning, monitoring, asset classification, internal controls, fraud, and large advances; it must be submitted to the bank's management and board within the timeline prescribed by RBI (typically by April 30).
The LFAR is a secret document submitted exclusively to the Income Tax Department to compute MAT.
The LFAR replaces the independent auditor's report under the Banking Regulation Act.
The LFAR is only required if a bank suffers a net loss exceeding ₹1,000 Crores.
questions.ref: RBI Circular on Revised LFAR Formats & ICAI Guidance Note on Bank Audit
questions.explanation: The LFAR is a structured questionnaire designed by the RBI requiring statutory branch and central auditors to provide detailed findings and qualitative evaluations on advances, cash management, clearing differences, compliance with RBI circulars, NPA identification, and internal control effectiveness.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Audit of Specific Entities: Banks, Insurance Companies, and Government Bodies
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Insurance Audit - Solvency Margin Requirement (IRDAI)
questions.question: Under IRDAI (Assets, Liabilities, and Solvency Margin of General Insurance Business) Regulations, what is the mandatory Minimum Solvency Ratio (Control Level of Solvency) that every insurer must maintain at all times?
options: A Solvency Ratio of not less than 1.50 (150% of the Required Solvency Margin).
A Solvency Ratio of not less than 1.00 (100%).
A Solvency Ratio of 2.50 for life insurers and 0.80 for general insurers.
Solvency margins are purely advisory and have no regulatory mandate.
questions.ref: IRDAI Regulations & Section 64VA of Insurance Act, 1938 - Solvency Margin
questions.explanation: Under Section 64VA of the Insurance Act, 1938 and IRDAI regulations, every insurer must maintain an excess of assets over liabilities known as the Solvency Margin. IRDAI has mandated a 'Control Level of Solvency' ratio of 1.50 (i.e. Available Solvency Margin / Required Solvency Margin ≥ 150%). If it falls below 1.50, the insurer must submit a financial restoration plan.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Audit of Specific Entities: Banks, Insurance Companies, and Government Bodies
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Insurance Audit - Unearned Premium Reserve (UPR)
questions.question: In the statutory audit of Suraksha General Insurance Ltd. for FY 2023-24, the auditor verifies the Reserve for Unexpired Risks (UPR) under Section 64V of the Insurance Act. For Fire, Marine Cargo, and Miscellaneous insurance policies, what are the statutory minimum percentages of net premium income required to be transferred to the UPR?
options: 50% of Net Premium Income for Fire and Miscellaneous business, and 100% of Net Premium Income for Marine Hull and Marine Cargo business.
25% across all general insurance lines of business.
100% for all policies regardless of line of business.
Zero, because insurance income is recognized on a cash receipt basis under IRDAI.
questions.ref: Section 64V of Insurance Act, 1938 & IRDAI (Preparation of Financial Statements) Regulations
questions.explanation: Under Section 64V of the Insurance Act, 1938 and IRDAI regulations, the reserve for unexpired risks is created at: (a) 50% of net premium income for Fire and Miscellaneous insurance business; and (b) 100% of net premium income for Marine Hull & Marine Cargo insurance business (reflecting longer voyaging risk profiles).

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Audit of Specific Entities: Banks, Insurance Companies, and Government Bodies
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Insurance Audit - Premium Received Before Risk Inception (Section 64VB)
questions.question: Under Section 64VB of the Insurance Act, 1938, what is the statutory prohibition regarding risk assumption by an insurer?
options: No risk can be assumed by the insurer unless and until the premium has been received in advance or guaranteed to be paid in such manner and within such time as prescribed.
Risk may be assumed immediately and premium collected up to 1 year after the policy expires.
Section 64VB only applies to foreign reinsurance companies.
Insurers can waive premium collection entirely for government officials.
questions.ref: Section 64VB of the Insurance Act, 1938 - No Risk to be Assumed unless Premium is Received in Advance
questions.explanation: Section 64VB of the Insurance Act, 1938 is a strict statutory provision stipulating that no insurer shall assume any risk in respect of any insurance business on which insurance permit is issued unless and until the premium payable is received by him or is guaranteed to be paid by such person in such manner and within such time as may be prescribed.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Audit of Specific Entities: Banks, Insurance Companies, and Government Bodies
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Government Audit - Constitutional Mandate of C&AG
questions.question: Under Articles 148 to 151 of the Constitution of India and the C&AG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971, what is the role and constitutional status of the Comptroller and Auditor General (C&AG) of India?
options: The C&AG is an independent constitutional authority appointed by the President of India who audits all receipts and expenditures of the Government of India, State Governments, and government corporations, and submits audit reports to the President/Governors to be laid before Parliament/State Legislatures.
The C&AG is an executive department under the direct administrative control of the Ministry of Finance.
The C&AG is an internal audit wing of the Reserve Bank of India.
The C&AG's reports are submitted to the Supreme Court for commercial arbitration.
questions.ref: Constitution of India, Articles 148-151 & C&AG DPC Act, 1971
questions.explanation: The C&AG is an independent constitutional authority established under Article 148 of the Constitution of India. Under Article 151, the C&AG submits audit reports relating to the accounts of the Union to the President, who causes them to be laid before each House of Parliament, where they are examined by the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) and Committee on Public Undertakings (COPU).

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Group Audits and the Work of Other Auditors
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 600 - Principal Auditor vs Component Auditor Responsibilities
questions.question: CA Ananya is the principal auditor of Global Horizons Ltd., which has 14 domestic subsidiaries and 2 foreign subsidiaries audited by different chartered accountancy firms. Under SA 600 'Using the Work of Another Auditor', what is Ananya's statutory responsibility and reporting practice regarding the financial statements of components audited by other auditors?
options: The principal auditor is entitled to rely on the work of the other auditor provided they exercise reasonable care and diligence; when the principal auditor bases their opinion on the group financial statements using the work of another auditor, they shall state in the auditor's report the extent to which the components' financial statements audited by other auditors have been included.
The principal auditor is strictly liable for any fraudulent misstatement in the subsidiaries even if audited by reputed separate firms.
The principal auditor must re-audit all subsidiary general ledgers line-by-line personally.
The principal auditor cannot issue an opinion on consolidated statements without obtaining prior permission from SEBI.
questions.ref: SA 600, Paragraphs 9, 10 & 14 - Principal Auditor Documentation & Reporting
questions.explanation: Under SA 600.9-14, the principal auditor can rely on the work of another auditor provided reasonable skill and care is exercised. When basing their opinion on financial information of components audited by other auditors, the auditor's report should express the division of responsibility by stating the extent to which the financial statements of components have been included and the fact that they were audited by other auditors.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Group Audits and the Work of Other Auditors
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 600 - Principal Auditor's Right to Inquire & Questionnaires
questions.question: Under SA 600, when planning to use the work of another auditor, what procedures should the principal auditor perform to evaluate the other auditor's work?
options: Advise the other auditor of the use that is to be made of their work and report, make sufficient arrangements for coordination, obtain a completed questionnaire regarding significant accounting and auditing matters, review written summaries of the other auditor's procedures, and consider significant findings.
Order the other auditor to transfer all confidential firm documentation permanently to the principal auditor.
Demand 50% of the audit fees collected by the component auditor.
Directly sue the component auditor's engagement partner in the High Court.
questions.ref: SA 600, Paragraphs 10, 11 & 12 - Procedures by the Principal Auditor
questions.explanation: Under SA 600.10-12, the principal auditor should: (a) Advise the other auditor of independence requirements and the use to be made of their work; (b) Obtain representation as to compliance with accounting, auditing, and reporting requirements; (c) Issue questionnaires/checklists; and (d) Review written summaries or discuss audit findings with the other auditor.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Group Audits and the Work of Other Auditors
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 610 (Revised) - Using the Work of Internal Auditors
questions.question: During the audit of a listed telecom company, the statutory audit team wants to use the internal audit department to perform physical verification of optical fiber assets and testing of IT general controls. Under SA 610 (Revised) 'Using the Work of Internal Auditors', what must the external auditor evaluate before deciding whether and to what extent the internal audit function can be used?
options: Evaluate the internal audit function's organizational status and objectivity, level of competence, and whether the function applies a systematic and disciplined approach (including quality control).
Verify whether the Chief Internal Auditor is related to the statutory audit partner.
Check whether internal auditors receive commissions on cost-cutting measures.
Internal audit work can never be used under any circumstances under ICAI standards.
questions.ref: SA 610 (Revised), Paragraph 15 - Evaluating the Internal Audit Function
questions.explanation: Under SA 610 (Revised).15, the external auditor shall determine whether the work of the internal audit function can be used by evaluating: (a) The extent to which the internal audit function's organizational status and relevant policies support the objectivity of the internal auditors; (b) The level of competence of the internal audit function; and (c) Whether the function applies a systematic and disciplined approach, including quality control.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Group Audits and the Work of Other Auditors
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 610 (Revised) - Prohibition of Direct Assistance
questions.question: Under the ICAI pronouncement on SA 610 (Revised) in India, what is the regulatory restriction regarding obtaining 'Direct Assistance' from internal auditors by external auditors in statutory audits of companies?
options: The Council of ICAI has prohibited statutory auditors in India from using internal auditors to provide 'direct assistance' in an audit of financial statements, because direct assistance impairs the external auditor's perceived independence and objectivity.
Direct assistance is mandatory and external auditors must delegate at least 40% of testing to internal staff.
Direct assistance is permitted only if approved in advance by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
Direct assistance is permitted only for computing corporate income tax liabilities.
questions.ref: ICAI Council Decision on SA 610 (Revised) - Ban on Direct Assistance from Internal Auditors in India
questions.explanation: The Council of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) has decided that the provisions of SA 610 (Revised) relating to using internal auditors to provide 'direct assistance' shall not be applicable in India. External statutory auditors cannot use internal audit staff to perform audit procedures under their direct direction, supervision, and review.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Group Audits and the Work of Other Auditors
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 620 - Using the Work of an Auditor's Expert
questions.question: In auditing the defined benefit pension obligation of a multinational enterprise under Ind AS 19, the engagement team engages an independent consulting actuary as an 'Auditor's Expert'. Under SA 620, what is the statutory auditor's ultimate responsibility regarding the audit opinion?
options: The auditor has sole responsibility for the audit opinion expressed, and that responsibility is not reduced by the auditor's use of the work of an auditor's expert.
The auditor's liability is transferred entirely to the actuary for all matters relating to employee benefit valuations.
The auditor must co-sign the audit report with the actuary as joint authors.
The auditor can disclaim responsibility by issuing an Other Matter Paragraph naming the actuary.
questions.ref: SA 620, Paragraph 3 - Responsibility for the Audit Opinion When Using an Expert
questions.explanation: Under SA 620.3, the auditor has sole responsibility for the audit opinion expressed, and that responsibility is not reduced by the auditor's use of the work of an auditor's expert. If the auditor concludes that the work of the expert is adequate for the auditor's purposes, the auditor may accept the expert's findings as appropriate audit evidence, but remains solely responsible for the opinion.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Group Audits and the Work of Other Auditors
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 620 - Reference to Expert in Auditor's Report
questions.question: Under SA 620, can the statutory auditor refer to the work of the auditor's expert in an auditor's report containing an UNMODIFIED opinion?
options: The auditor shall not refer to the work of an auditor's expert in an auditor's report containing an unmodified opinion unless required by law or regulation to do so.
Yes, the auditor must always name the expert in the introductory paragraph.
Yes, provided the expert gives a written clearance letter.
Only if the expert's fee exceeded ₹50 Lakhs.
questions.ref: SA 620, Paragraphs 14 & 15 - Reference to the Auditor's Expert in the Auditor's Report
questions.explanation: Under SA 620.14, the auditor shall not refer to the work of an auditor's expert in an auditor's report containing an unmodified opinion unless required by law or regulation to do so. If such reference is required by law, the auditor shall indicate that the reference does not reduce the auditor's responsibility for the opinion. (Reference is permitted in a modified opinion only if relevant to understanding the modification).

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Group Audits and the Work of Other Auditors
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Group Audits - Consolidation Adjustments Verification
questions.question: In auditing Consolidated Financial Statements (CFS) under Section 129(3) and Ind AS 110, what specific consolidation adjustments must the group auditor verify?
options: Elimination of intragroup balances, transactions, income, and expenses; unrealized profits on downstream and upstream asset sales; uniform accounting policies adjustments; purchase price allocation (PPA); goodwill computation; and non-controlling interest (NCI) allocation.
Only the arithmetic addition of individual balance sheets without eliminating intragroup transactions.
Conversion of all rupee figures into US dollars at historical exchange rates.
Verification of directors' travel expenses across group subsidiaries.
questions.ref: ICAI Guidance Note on Audit of Consolidated Financial Statements & Ind AS 110
questions.explanation: The group auditor must specifically audit the consolidation adjustments process under Ind AS 110, including: complete elimination of intragroup balances and transactions, elimination of unrealized profits/losses, adjustments for uniform accounting policies, determination of goodwill/gain on bargain purchase, amortization/impairment, and fair value allocations at acquisition date.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Group Audits and the Work of Other Auditors
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 620 - Evaluating Adequacy of Expert's Work
questions.question: When evaluating the adequacy of the auditor's expert's work under SA 620, which of the following is the auditor required to evaluate?
options: The relevance and reasonableness of the expert's findings and conclusions, consistency with other audit evidence, the relevance and reasonableness of significant assumptions and methods used, and the relevance, completeness, and accuracy of source data used by the expert.
Whether the expert is a registered voter in the company's home state.
The expert's university grade point average from undergraduate studies.
Whether the expert's office building is insured against earthquakes.
questions.ref: SA 620, Paragraph 12 - Evaluating the Adequacy of the Auditor's Expert's Work
questions.explanation: Under SA 620.12, the auditor shall evaluate the adequacy of the auditor's expert's work for the auditor's purposes, including: (a) The relevance and reasonableness of that expert's findings or conclusions, and their consistency with other audit evidence; (b) If that expert's work involves use of significant assumptions and methods, the relevance and reasonableness of those assumptions and methods; and (c) If that expert's work involves the use of source data that is significant, the relevance, completeness, and accuracy of that source data.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Group Audits and the Work of Other Auditors
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Group Audits - Component Materiality
questions.question: In a group audit engagement involving multiple operating subsidiaries, how should component materiality be determined?
options: Component materiality must be set at an amount lower than the group financial statements materiality as a whole to reduce aggregation risk across different components.
Component materiality must always be identical to group materiality.
Component materiality must be double the group materiality.
Component materiality is determined exclusively by the managing director of each subsidiary.
questions.ref: ICAI CA Final Study Material & Standards on Group Audits - Component Materiality
questions.explanation: To address aggregation risk (the risk that uncorrected and undetected misstatements in individual components, when aggregated across the group, could exceed group materiality), component materiality must be established at an amount lower than group materiality.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 705 (Revised) - Material vs Pervasive Misstatements
questions.question: Under SA 705 (Revised) 'Modifications to the Opinion in the Independent Auditor's Report', which opinion must the auditor express when financial statements are materially misstated AND the effects are PERVASIVE?
options: Adverse Opinion.
Qualified Opinion.
Disclaimer of Opinion.
Unmodified Opinion with an Emphasis of Matter paragraph.
questions.ref: SA 705 (Revised), Paragraph 8 - Adverse Opinion Criteria
questions.explanation: Under SA 705 (Revised).8, the auditor shall express an Adverse Opinion when the auditor, having obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence, concludes that misstatements, individually or in the aggregate, are both material AND pervasive to the financial statements.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 705 (Revised) - Inability to Obtain SAAE (Disclaimer)
questions.question: Due to seizure of all accounting servers and physical books by enforcement agencies, the auditor of Horizon Enterprises Ltd. is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence across all operational, revenue, and banking cycles. The possible effects of undetected misstatements are material and pervasive. What opinion must the auditor express?
options: Disclaimer of Opinion.
Qualified Opinion.
Adverse Opinion.
Clean Unmodified Opinion with a note in CARO.
questions.ref: SA 705 (Revised), Paragraph 9 - Disclaimer of Opinion Criteria
questions.explanation: Under SA 705 (Revised).9, the auditor shall disclaim an opinion when the auditor is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence on which to base the opinion (limitation on scope), and the auditor concludes that the possible effects on the financial statements of undetected misstatements, if any, could be both material and pervasive.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 701 - Key Audit Matters (KAM) vs Modified Opinion
questions.question: Under SA 701 'Communicating Key Audit Matters in the Independent Auditor's Report', if a matter gives rise to a modified audit opinion (e.g. qualified or adverse opinion under SA 705), can that matter be reported in the Key Audit Matters section?
options: No. SA 701 explicitly prohibits communicating a matter giving rise to a modified opinion in the Key Audit Matters section; such matters are reported exclusively in the 'Basis for Modification' section, with a cross-reference in the KAM section.
Yes, all modified opinion matters must be duplicated word-for-word in the KAM section.
Only if approved by the National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA).
Yes, because KAM is meant for negative findings only.
questions.ref: SA 701, Paragraph 15 - Interaction Between KAM and Modified Opinions (SA 705)
questions.explanation: Under SA 701.15, a matter giving rise to a modified opinion in accordance with SA 705 is by its nature a key audit matter. However, such matters shall not be described in the Key Audit Matters section; instead, the auditor shall report them in accordance with SA 705 in the Basis for Opinion section and include a reference in the KAM section pointing to the Basis for Modification section.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 706 (Revised) - Emphasis of Matter (EOM) Paragraph
questions.question: Under SA 706 (Revised), what is the strict prerequisite before an auditor can include an Emphasis of Matter (EOM) paragraph in the auditor's report?
options: The matter must be fundamental to users' understanding of the financial statements AND must be appropriately presented or disclosed in the financial statements, and is not required to be modified under SA 705 or determined to be a KAM under SA 701.
The matter must be a secret fraud that management refused to disclose in the accounts.
The client must have achieved record profits during the year.
The auditor must be resigning from practice within 30 days.
questions.ref: SA 706 (Revised), Paragraph 6 - Conditions for Including an Emphasis of Matter Paragraph
questions.explanation: Under SA 706 (Revised).6, the auditor shall include an Emphasis of Matter paragraph provided: (a) The auditor would not be required to modify the opinion under SA 705 as a result of the matter; (b) The matter has not been determined to be a Key Audit Matter to be communicated in the auditor's report under SA 701; and (c) The matter is appropriately presented or disclosed in the financial statements.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] CARO 2020 - Clause (i)(c) Title Deeds of Immovable Property
questions.question: Under Clause (i)(c) of Paragraph 3 of CARO 2020, what is the auditor's reporting duty regarding title deeds of immovable properties?
options: Report whether the title deeds of all immovable properties (other than properties where the company is the lessee and lease agreements are duly executed) disclosed in financial statements are held in the name of the company; if not, provide specified tabular details including description, gross carrying value, held in whose name, relationship with promoter/director, and period held.
Verify only whether municipal property taxes were paid before March 31.
Auditors are only required to inspect property title deeds if requested by the local land registry.
Title deed verification is only required for agricultural land.
questions.ref: CARO 2020, Paragraph 3, Clause (i)(c) - Title Deeds of Immovable Property
questions.explanation: Under CARO 2020 Clause (i)(c), the auditor must report whether the title deeds of all immovable properties (other than properties where the company is the lessee and lease agreements are executed) are held in the name of the company. If not, the auditor must provide details in a structured table specifying description, gross value, name of holder, relationship with promoters/directors, reason for not being held in company name, and dispute status.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] CARO 2020 - Clause (ii)(b) Quarterly Stock Statements vs Books
questions.question: Under Clause (ii)(b) of CARO 2020, if a company has been sanctioned working capital limits in excess of ₹5 Crores from banks or financial institutions on the basis of security of current assets, what must the auditor report?
options: Whether quarterly returns or statements filed by the company with such banks or financial institutions are in agreement with the books of account of the company; if not, give details.
Whether the bank manager has visited the warehouse in each quarter.
Whether the company pays loan interest at repo rate or reverse repo rate.
Whether the company has mortgaged the residential flats of its directors.
questions.ref: CARO 2020, Paragraph 3, Clause (ii)(b) - Discrepancies in Working Capital Quarterly Filings
questions.explanation: Under CARO 2020 Clause (ii)(b), whether during any point of time of the year, the company has been sanctioned working capital limits in excess of five crore rupees, in aggregate, from banks or financial institutions on the basis of security of current assets; whether the quarterly returns or statements filed by the company with such banks or financial institutions are in agreement with the books of account of the company of the respective quarters; and if not, give details.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] CARO 2020 - Clause (ix)(b) Wilful Defaulter Reporting
questions.question: Under Clause (ix)(b) of CARO 2020, what must the statutory auditor report regarding wilful default?
options: Whether the company is a declared wilful defaulter by any bank or financial institution or other lender.
Whether any customer of the company has failed to pay an invoice within 30 days.
Whether directors of the company have defaulted on their personal credit cards.
Wilful default can only be reported under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code.
questions.ref: CARO 2020, Paragraph 3, Clause (ix)(b) - Declared Wilful Defaulter
questions.explanation: Under CARO 2020 Clause (ix)(b), the auditor is required to report whether the company is a declared wilful defaulter by any bank or financial institution or other lender in accordance with RBI guidelines.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] CARO 2020 - Clause (xi)(c) Whistle-Blower Complaints
questions.question: Under Clause (xi)(c) of CARO 2020, what is the auditor's specific reporting requirement regarding whistle-blowers?
options: Whether the auditor has considered whistle-blower complaints, if any, received during the year by the company.
The auditor must disclose the identity and personal address of every whistle-blower.
The auditor must award monetary compensation to whistle-blowers from audit fees.
Whistle-blower complaints can only be considered by the Central Vigilance Commission.
questions.ref: CARO 2020, Paragraph 3, Clause (xi)(c) - Whistle-Blower Complaints Consideration
questions.explanation: Under CARO 2020 Clause (xi)(c), the auditor must report whether the auditor has considered whistle-blower complaints, if any, received during the year by the company. The auditor evaluates complaints received via vigil mechanisms and assesses financial and fraud implications.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Audit Documentation, Reporting, and Modified Audit Opinions
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] CARO 2020 - Clause (xix) Financial Viability & Ratio Analysis
questions.question: Under Clause (xix) of CARO 2020, what critical professional assessment must the auditor report regarding the company's financial viability?
options: On the basis of financial ratios, ageing and expected dates of realization of financial assets and payment of financial liabilities, other information accompanying the financial statements, and the auditor's knowledge of the Board and management plans, whether the auditor is of the opinion that no material uncertainty exists that the company is capable of meeting its liabilities existing at the date of balance sheet as and when they fall due within a period of one year from the balance sheet date.
Whether the company will make profits for the next 10 years guaranteed.
Whether the share price will double in the next fiscal year.
Clause (xix) only applies to Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs).
questions.ref: CARO 2020, Paragraph 3, Clause (xix) - Capability to Meet Liabilities Falling Due Within 1 Year
questions.explanation: Under CARO 2020 Clause (xix), the auditor must evaluate financial ratios, ageing, realization timelines, and board plans to state whether the auditor is of the opinion that no material uncertainty exists as of the date of the audit report that the company is capable of meeting its liabilities existing at the date of balance sheet as and when they fall due within a period of one year from the balance sheet date.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Assurance Engagements and Attestation Services
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SRE 2410 - Review of Interim Financial Information
questions.question: Under SRE 2410 'Review of Interim Financial Information Performed by the Independent Auditor of the Entity', what is the fundamental nature of procedures performed by the practitioner, and what form of assurance is expressed?
options: Procedures consist primarily of making inquiries (primarily of persons responsible for financial and accounting matters) and applying analytical and other review procedures; the practitioner expresses Moderate / Limited Assurance in negative form ('nothing has come to our attention...').
Procedures require 100% substantive vouching of all invoices; the practitioner expresses absolute assurance.
Procedures are identical to a statutory audit under SA 700; positive reasonable assurance is expressed.
The practitioner expresses no assurance and only stamps the trial balance.
questions.ref: SRE 2410, Paragraphs 9 & 15 - Nature of Review Procedures and Form of Conclusion
questions.explanation: Under SRE 2410, an interim review is substantially less in scope than an audit conducted in accordance with Standards on Auditing and does not enable the auditor to obtain assurance that the auditor would become aware of all significant matters. The procedures comprise inquiry and analytical procedures, yielding limited assurance expressed in negative form: 'Nothing has come to our attention that causes us to believe that the accompanying interim financial information does not give a true and fair view...'.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Assurance Engagements and Attestation Services
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SAE 3400 - Examination of Prospective Financial Information (PFI)
questions.question: Under SAE 3400 'The Examination of Prospective Financial Information', what is the vital distinction between a 'Forecast' and a 'Projection'?
options: A Forecast is PFI prepared on the basis of assumptions as to future events which management expects to take place (best-estimate assumptions); a Projection is PFI prepared on the basis of hypothetical assumptions about future events or a mixture of best-estimate and hypothetical assumptions ('what-if' scenarios).
A Forecast is prepared for 10 years, while a Projection is prepared for 1 month.
A Forecast is prepared by the auditor, while a Projection is prepared by the banker.
There is no distinction; both terms mean historical financial statements.
questions.ref: SAE 3400, Paragraphs 3 & 4 - Definitions of Forecast and Projection
questions.explanation: Under SAE 3400.3-4: (a) 'Forecast' means prospective financial information prepared on the basis of assumptions as to future events which management expects to take place and the actions management expects to take as of the date the information is prepared (best-estimate assumptions); (b) 'Projection' means prospective financial information prepared on the basis of hypothetical assumptions about future events and management actions, or a mixture of best-estimate and hypothetical assumptions.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Assurance Engagements and Attestation Services
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SAE 3400 - Auditor's Opinion on Prospective Information
questions.question: Can an auditor express an opinion that the results forecasted or projected in Prospective Financial Information (PFI) WILL BE ACHIEVED?
options: No. Under SAE 3400, the auditor cannot express an opinion as to whether the results will be achieved because events and circumstances frequently do not occur as expected and differences between actual results and PFI are often material.
Yes, if the auditor charges a success fee tied to the company's future profit.
Yes, provided management provides a counter-indemnity on judicial stamp paper.
Yes, if the forecast is prepared using automated artificial intelligence software.
questions.ref: SAE 3400, Paragraph 9 - Inability to Express Opinion on Achievement of Results
questions.explanation: Under SAE 3400.9, the auditor should not express an opinion on whether the results predicted in the PFI will be achieved. The auditor's examination report states whether anything has come to the auditor's attention to cause the auditor to believe that the assumptions do not provide a reasonable basis for the PFI, and provides an explicit warning that actual results are likely to differ from PFI.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Assurance Engagements and Attestation Services
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SAE 3402 - Type 1 vs Type 2 Assurance Reports on Service Organizations
questions.question: Under SAE 3402 'Assurance Reports on Controls at a Service Organization', what is the critical difference in the scope and period covered between a Type 1 and a Type 2 report?
options: A Type 1 report opines on the description and design suitability of service organization controls as of a specific date only; a Type 2 report opines on description, design suitability, AND operating effectiveness of controls throughout a specified period (ordinarily not less than 6 months).
Type 1 is issued by internal auditors, while Type 2 is issued by the High Court.
Type 1 covers cloud security, while Type 2 covers employee provident funds.
Type 1 is issued for private companies, while Type 2 is issued only for public banks.
questions.ref: SAE 3402, Paragraph 9 - Type 1 and Type 2 Assurance Reports
questions.explanation: Under SAE 3402.9: (1) Type 1 report: Report on description and design of controls at a service organization as of a specified point in time; (2) Type 2 report: Report on description, design suitability, AND operating effectiveness of controls throughout a specified period (typically 6 to 12 months), including detailed tests of controls and results.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Assurance Engagements and Attestation Services
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SRS 4400 (Revised) - Agreed-Upon Procedures (AUP) Engagements
questions.question: Under SRS 4400 (Revised) 'Engagements to Perform Agreed-Upon Procedures Regarding Financial Information', what form of assurance is expressed by the practitioner?
options: NO assurance is expressed; the practitioner merely issues a report of factual findings resulting from the specific procedures agreed with the engaging party, allowing users to draw their own conclusions.
Positive reasonable assurance (true and fair view).
Negative limited assurance ('nothing has come to our attention').
Absolute forensic certification.
questions.ref: SRS 4400 (Revised), Paragraph 6 - Nature of Agreed-Upon Procedures Report
questions.explanation: Under SRS 4400 (Revised).6, an agreed-upon procedures engagement involves performing procedures agreed between the practitioner and the engaging party and reporting factual findings. The practitioner does NOT express an audit opinion or review conclusion (i.e. zero assurance is expressed). Users of the report assess for themselves the procedures and findings and draw their own conclusions.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Assurance Engagements and Attestation Services
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SRS 4410 (Revised) - Compilation Engagements
questions.question: Under SRS 4410 (Revised) 'Compilation Engagements', what is the role and responsibility of the professional accountant in compiling financial statements for a client?
options: The practitioner applies accounting and financial reporting expertise to assist management in the preparation and presentation of financial information without undertaking to obtain any assurance on that information.
The practitioner audits all records and guarantees zero fraud in the compilation report.
The practitioner becomes a full partner in the client's business enterprise.
Compilation engagements can only be conducted by advocates enrolled in the Bar Council.
questions.ref: SRS 4410 (Revised), Paragraph 5 - Objective of Compilation Engagement
questions.explanation: Under SRS 4410 (Revised).5, the practitioner's objective in a compilation engagement is to apply accounting and financial reporting expertise to assist management in the preparation and presentation of financial information in accordance with an applicable financial reporting framework, without undertaking to obtain any audit or review assurance.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Assurance Engagements and Attestation Services
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SAE 3420 - Pro Forma Financial Information in a Prospectus
questions.question: Under SAE 3420 'Assurance Engagements to Report on the Compilation of Pro Forma Financial Information Included in a Prospectus', what is the practitioner's objective when examining pro forma financial statements for an IPO / Rights Issue?
options: Obtain reasonable assurance about whether the pro forma financial information has been compiled, in all material respects, by the responsible party on the basis of the applicable criteria and whether pro forma adjustments give appropriate effect to the specified event or transaction.
Predict whether the company's shares will list at a premium on the Bombay Stock Exchange.
Guarantee the future quarterly dividends of the company for the next 5 years.
Verify whether the underwriting syndicate has deposited the issue money in escrow.
questions.ref: SAE 3420, Paragraph 6 - Purpose of Pro Forma Assurance Engagement
