questions.explanation: Under SAE 3420.6, the practitioner's objective is to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the pro forma financial information has been compiled, in all material respects, by the responsible party on the basis of the applicable criteria. This involves evaluating whether pro forma adjustments give appropriate effect to the transaction and whether the pro forma column reflects proper application of adjustments to unadjusted financial information.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Assurance Engagements and Attestation Services
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Framework for Assurance Engagements - Elements of Assurance Engagement
questions.question: Under the ICAI Framework for Assurance Engagements, which of the following lists the FIVE essential elements of any assurance engagement?
options: A three-party relationship (practitioner, responsible party, and intended users), an appropriate subject matter, suitable criteria, sufficient appropriate evidence, and a written assurance report.
An auditor, a lawyer, a banker, a police officer, and a judge.
Assets, Liabilities, Income, Expenses, and Equity.
Planning, Testing, Invoicing, Collection, and Archiving.
questions.ref: ICAI Framework for Assurance Engagements - Paragraph 20 (Five Elements of Assurance)
questions.explanation: Under the Framework for Assurance Engagements, every assurance engagement comprises five elements: (1) A three-party relationship involving a practitioner, a responsible party, and intended users; (2) An appropriate subject matter; (3) Suitable criteria; (4) Sufficient appropriate evidence; and (5) A written assurance report in the form appropriate to a reasonable assurance engagement or a limited assurance engagement.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Assurance Engagements and Attestation Services
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SRE 2400 (Revised) - Engagements to Review Historical Financial Statements
questions.question: Under SRE 2400 (Revised) 'Engagements to Review Historical Financial Statements', when can a practitioner accept a review engagement of financial statements?
options: When the practitioner determines that a review engagement would satisfy the intended purpose, ethical requirements including independence are met, and the preconditions for a review are present.
Only if the client's annual revenue is less than ₹10 Lakhs.
A review engagement can never be performed for historical financial statements.
Only if the practitioner is given power of attorney over the client's bank accounts.
questions.ref: SRE 2400 (Revised), Paragraphs 29-31 - Acceptance of Review Engagements
questions.explanation: Under SRE 2400 (Revised), a practitioner may accept a review engagement of historical financial statements when: (a) Ethical requirements, including independence, are complied with; (b) The practitioner has determined that a review engagement is appropriate; and (c) Preconditions for a review engagement are present (applicable reporting framework, management's agreement to responsibilities).

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Internal Audit and Forensic Audit
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Section 138 - Mandatory Internal Audit Applicability Limits
questions.question: Under Section 138 of the Companies Act, 2013 read with Rule 13 of the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014, which of the following unlisted public companies is MANDATORILY required to appoint an internal auditor?
options: Every unlisted public company having: (a) Paid-up share capital of ₹50 Crores or more during preceding FY; OR (b) Turnover of ₹200 Crores or more during preceding FY; OR (c) Outstanding loans or borrowings from banks or financial institutions exceeding ₹100 Crores at any point of time during preceding FY; OR (d) Outstanding deposits of ₹25 Crores or more at any point of time during preceding FY.
Every unlisted public company having paid-up capital of ₹10 Crores or turnover of ₹50 Crores.
Only unlisted public companies that have defaulted on bank interest payments.
All unlisted public companies are exempt from Section 138.
questions.ref: Section 138 of Companies Act, 2013 & Rule 13 of Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014
questions.explanation: Under Section 138 and Rule 13, mandatory internal audit applies to: (1) Every listed company; (2) Unlisted public company if: Paid up capital ≥ ₹50 Cr, Turnover ≥ ₹200 Cr, Outstanding loans/borrowings > ₹100 Cr, or Outstanding deposits ≥ ₹25 Cr; (3) Private company if: Turnover ≥ ₹200 Cr, or Outstanding loans/borrowings > ₹100 Cr.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Internal Audit and Forensic Audit
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Section 143(12) - Reporting of Fraud to Central Government (Form ADT-4)
questions.question: During statutory audit of a company, the auditor uncovers a procurement kickback fraud involving the Head of Procurement and an external vendor, resulting in an estimated misappropriation of ₹1.80 Crores. Under Section 143(12) of the Companies Act, 2013 read with Rule 13 of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014, what is the mandatory reporting timeline and procedure?
options: Report the matter to the Board/Audit Committee within 2 days seeking reply within 45 days. On receipt of reply (or if no reply received within 45 days), forward the report in Form ADT-4 to the Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Central Government within 15 days.
Report the matter only in the confidential notes to the local police station within 24 hours.
Wait until the next Annual General Meeting and report verbally to shareholders.
Since the amount is less than ₹10 Crores, report only to the Managing Director.
questions.ref: Section 143(12) of Companies Act, 2013 & Rule 13 of Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014
questions.explanation: Under Section 143(12) and Rule 13, if an auditor has reason to believe that an offence of fraud involving an amount of ₹1 Crore or above is being or has been committed against the company by its officers or employees, the auditor shall: (1) Report to the Board/Audit Committee within 2 days seeking their reply within 45 days; and (2) Within 15 days of receiving reply (or after 45 days if no reply is received), forward the report in Form ADT-4 to the Central Government (MCA).

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Internal Audit and Forensic Audit
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Forensic Audit vs Statutory Audit Differences
questions.question: How does a Forensic Audit fundamentally differ from a Statutory Audit in objective, approach, and mindset?
options: A statutory audit determines whether financial statements present a true and fair view with reasonable assurance and professional skepticism, working on a sample basis; whereas a forensic audit specifically investigates suspected financial crimes, fraud, or asset diversion to establish legal evidence for prosecution, using an investigative mindset, deeper verification, and non-sampling techniques.
A statutory audit is conducted for courts, while a forensic audit is for tax authorities.
A statutory audit looks only at future budgets, while a forensic audit looks at past bank records.
There is no difference; statutory auditors are legally required to perform full forensic audits.
questions.ref: ICAI Forensic Accounting and Investigation Standards (FAIS) - Conceptual Framework
questions.explanation: A statutory audit is a compliance and assurance engagement evaluating financial statements on a test/sampling basis with reasonable assurance. A forensic audit is an investigative assignment aimed at gathering admissible evidence of financial fraud, tracing stolen assets, quantifying damages, and establishing culpability in legal proceedings.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Internal Audit and Forensic Audit
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Forensic Audit - Fraud Triangle & Fraud Diamond
questions.question: In forensic investigation, what are the three elements of Cressey's 'Fraud Triangle', and what fourth element was added by Wolfe and Hermanson to form the 'Fraud Diamond'?
options: Fraud Triangle: Pressure (Incentive), Opportunity, and Rationalization; Fraud Diamond adds: Capability (the individual's traits and abilities to actually commit and conceal the fraud).
Fraud Triangle: Greed, Revenge, and Power; Fraud Diamond adds: Weapon.
Fraud Triangle: Revenue, Expense, and Asset; Fraud Diamond adds: Liability.
Fraud Triangle: Lawyer, Judge, and Police; Fraud Diamond adds: Prisoner.
questions.ref: ICAI FAIS Standards & Fraud Theory - Fraud Triangle and Fraud Diamond
questions.explanation: Donald Cressey's Fraud Triangle posits that three elements must be present for occupational fraud: (1) Pressure/Incentive; (2) Opportunity (e.g. weak internal controls); and (3) Rationalization (justification of wrongdoing). The Fraud Diamond (Wolfe & Hermanson) adds Capability—the person must possess the knowledge, position, ego, and resilience to execute and conceal the fraud.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Internal Audit and Forensic Audit
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Forensic Techniques - Benford's Law Analysis
questions.question: How is Benford's Law (First Digit Law) applied as an analytical technique in forensic audits to detect fabricated financial data?
options: In naturally occurring numerical datasets, the probability that the leading first digit is '1' is approximately 30.1%, '2' is 17.6%, down to '9' at 4.6%; significant deviations from this logarithmic distribution indicate anomalous, manipulated, or artificially created numbers.
It requires all ledger transactions to be rounded off to the nearest thousand rupees.
It assumes every digit from 1 to 9 has an equal 11.11% probability of occurrence.
It is an algorithm used exclusively to calculate compound interest on loans.
questions.ref: ICAI FAIS Standard 310 - Using Data Analytics & Benford's Law in Forensic Investigations
questions.explanation: Benford's Law states that in naturally occurring numerical datasets, smaller digits appear as the leading first digit far more frequently than larger digits (P(d) = log10(1 + 1/d)). Since human fraudsters randomly invent numbers with a uniform distribution or target specific approval limits (e.g. ₹4,999), Benford's Law flags anomalous spikes.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Internal Audit and Forensic Audit
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Section 138 - Who Can Be Appointed as Internal Auditor?
questions.question: Under Section 138(1) of the Companies Act, 2013, who is legally eligible to be appointed as an Internal Auditor of a company?
options: A Chartered Accountant (whether in practice or not), or a Cost Accountant, or such other professional as may be decided by the Board, and such internal auditor may or may not be an employee of the company.
Only a Chartered Accountant holding a Certificate of Practice (COP) from ICAI.
Only the Statutory Auditor of the company.
Only a retired officer from the Ministry of Finance.
questions.ref: Section 138(1) of Companies Act, 2013 - Eligibility of Internal Auditor
questions.explanation: Under Section 138(1), an internal auditor shall either be a chartered accountant (whether engaged in practice or not) or a cost accountant, or such other professional as may be decided by the Board to conduct internal audit of the functions and activities of the company. The internal auditor may be an employee of the company or an external firm.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Internal Audit and Forensic Audit
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Forensic Audit - Digital Evidence & Chain of Custody
questions.question: Under ICAI Forensic Accounting and Investigation Standards (FAIS 320) and the Indian Evidence Act / Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, what is 'Chain of Custody' for digital forensic evidence?
options: A documented chronological record showing the seizure, custody, control, transfer, analysis, and disposition of physical and electronic evidence to prove that evidence has not been altered, tampered with, or substituted.
The physical chain used to padlock the forensic auditor's briefcase.
A blockchain smart contract recording Bitcoin transactions.
A list of police constables on duty at the court premises.
questions.ref: ICAI FAIS 320 - Evidence and Documentation & Chain of Custody
questions.explanation: Chain of Custody is a crucial legal and forensic process demonstrating that digital/physical evidence seized during an investigation was preserved in its pristine state without tampering. It records who collected it, when, how it was hashed (MD5/SHA-256), where it was stored, and who accessed it, ensuring admissibility in a court of law.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Internal Audit and Forensic Audit
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Standards on Internal Audit (SIA) - SIA 210
questions.question: Under Standard on Internal Audit (SIA) 210 'Managing the Internal Audit Function' issued by ICAI, what is the core responsibility of the Chief Internal Auditor (Chief Audit Executive)?
options: Develop a risk-based internal audit plan, ensure adequate resources, maintain independence and objectivity, report directly to the Audit Committee/Board functionally, and implement a quality assurance and improvement program.
Authorize all commercial purchase orders on behalf of executive management.
Prepare the monthly goods and services tax (GST) returns of the company.
Sign the company's annual financial statements on behalf of the Board.
questions.ref: ICAI Standard on Internal Audit (SIA) 210 - Managing Internal Audit Function
questions.explanation: Under SIA 210, the Head of Internal Audit is responsible for effectively managing the internal audit function to ensure it adds value to the organization. Key duties include formulating a risk-based internal audit plan aligned with organizational goals, ensuring independence (functional reporting to Audit Committee), resource allocation, and quality assurance.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Internal Audit and Forensic Audit
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Forensic Techniques - Forensic Interviewing & Kinesic Analysis
questions.question: In a forensic accounting investigation, how does an 'investigative interview' differ from an ordinary audit inquiry?
options: An investigative interview is a structured, psychologically calibrated dialogue designed to obtain factual admissions, detect verbal and non-verbal deception (kinesic behavior), evaluate inconsistencies, and secure written confessions or corroborative leads.
An investigative interview is conducted under police hypnosis in a hospital.
An investigative interview is a friendly informal chat with coffee and no notes.
Investigative interviews are strictly prohibited under Indian corporate law.
questions.ref: ICAI FAIS 330 - Conducting Interviews in Forensic Engagements
questions.explanation: Under FAIS 330, interviews in forensic assignments are structured into distinct stages: introductory, informational, assessment, and admission-seeking (if appropriate). The investigator carefully observes verbal clues, cognitive load, and non-verbal kinesic indicators to uncover concealed transactions and establish motive and modus operandi.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Due Diligence and Special Purpose Audits
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Due Diligence - Financial Due Diligence Objectives
questions.question: In an acquisition transaction, a private equity investor engages a Chartered Accountant firm to perform Financial Due Diligence (FDD) on the target entity. What is the core focus of Financial Due Diligence compared to a regular audit?
options: FDD evaluates the Quality of Earnings (QoE), Quality of Net Assets, sustainability of historical EBITDA, normalized working capital requirements, hidden debt or off-balance sheet commitments, and tax contingencies to assist the buyer in valuation and transaction structuring.
FDD is designed solely to issue a statutory true and fair view audit opinion for the Registrar of Companies.
FDD guarantees that the buyer's stock price will rise after acquisition.
FDD only verifies the arithmetic totals of the target's electricity bills.
questions.ref: ICAI Guidance Note on Due Diligence - Financial Due Diligence Scope & Objectives
questions.explanation: Financial Due Diligence is a commercial investigation designed to help an acquirer or investor understand the target's historical financial reality. It focuses on Quality of Earnings (identifying non-recurring items to calculate 'Normalized EBITDA'), debt-like items, normalized working capital, potential unrecorded liabilities, and tax risks to inform the deal valuation and purchase agreement clauses (reps & warranties).

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Due Diligence and Special Purpose Audits
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Due Diligence - Quality of Earnings (QoE) & Normalized EBITDA
questions.question: During financial due diligence of a target pharmaceutical manufacturer with reported EBITDA of ₹50 Crores, the investigator identifies: (1) Gain on sale of surplus factory land: ₹8 Crores; (2) Below-market director compensation of ₹1 Crore (fair market salary: ₹3 Crores); (3) One-off insurance compensation for cyclone damage: ₹4 Crores. What is the Normalized (Adjusted) EBITDA of the target for valuation purposes?
options: Normalized EBITDA = ₹36 Crores (Reported ₹50 Cr - Land gain ₹8 Cr - Insurance gain ₹4 Cr - Extra director compensation ₹2 Cr).
Normalized EBITDA = ₹50 Crores (No adjustments permitted to audited figures).
Normalized EBITDA = ₹62 Crores (All items added to EBITDA).
Normalized EBITDA = ₹42 Crores.
questions.ref: ICAI Guidance Note on Due Diligence - EBITDA Normalization Adjustments
questions.explanation: Normalized EBITDA eliminates non-recurring, non-operational, and non-arm's length items to reflect ongoing earnings: Reported EBITDA (₹50 Cr) - One-off Land Gain (₹8 Cr) - One-off Insurance Gain (₹4 Cr) - Incremental Arm's Length Director Salary (₹3 Cr - ₹1 Cr = ₹2 Cr) = ₹50 - 8 - 4 - 2 = ₹36 Crores.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Due Diligence and Special Purpose Audits
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Section 142(2A) - Special Audit Under the Income Tax Act
questions.question: Under Section 142(2A) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, when can the Assessing Officer direct the assessee to get accounts audited by an accountant (Chartered Accountant nominated by the Principal Chief Commissioner/Chief Commissioner)?
options: Having regard to the nature and complexity of accounts, volume of accounts, doubts about correctness of accounts, multiplicity of transactions, or specialized nature of business activity, and the interests of revenue, with previous approval of the Principal Chief Commissioner or Commissioner.
Whenever the assessee refuses to pay advance tax.
Whenever the assessee's gross turnover exceeds ₹10 Lakhs.
Special audit under Section 142(2A) is conducted only for salaried government employees.
questions.ref: Section 142(2A) of Income Tax Act, 1961 - Special Audit Mandate
questions.explanation: Under Section 142(2A), if the Assessing Officer, at any stage of proceedings before him, having regard to the nature and complexity of the accounts, volume of accounts, doubts about correctness of accounts, multiplicity of transactions, or specialized nature of business activity, and the interests of the revenue, is of the opinion that it is necessary, he may, with prior approval of Principal Chief Commissioner/Commissioner, direct the assessee to get accounts audited by a nominated CA.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Due Diligence and Special Purpose Audits
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Due Diligence - Hidden Liabilities & Off-Balance Sheet Exposures
questions.question: In performing due diligence on a target engineering company, which of the following areas is most prone to containing 'Hidden Liabilities' not reflected on the face of the balance sheet?
options: Pending litigation and unquantified show-cause notices from tax/customs authorities, non-compete agreements with disputed earnouts, environmental remediation obligations, unfunded post-retirement benefits, and corporate cross-guarantees issued for sister entities.
Cash held in current account with the State Bank of India.
Paid-up equity share capital shown under Shareholder Funds.
Trade debtors less than 15 days old.
questions.ref: ICAI Guidance Note on Due Diligence - Review of Hidden and Contingent Liabilities
questions.explanation: Due diligence specifically scrutinizes hidden and contingent liabilities, such as: pending excise/customs/GST disputes, show-cause notices, environmental contamination liabilities, product warranty claims, change-of-control golden parachute severance clauses, and third-party bank guarantees that could crystallize post-closing.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Due Diligence and Special Purpose Audits
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Peer Review vs Quality Review (QRB)
questions.question: What is the distinction between 'Peer Review' conducted by ICAI's Peer Review Board and 'Quality Review' conducted by the Quality Review Board (QRB)?
options: Peer Review is an internal self-regulatory mechanism of ICAI focused on evaluating a practice unit's quality control systems and compliance with technical standards; Quality Review is an independent statutory body established under Section 28A of the CA Act (dominated by government nominees) to review quality of services of CAs and make recommendations to Council.
Peer Review is conducted by the police, while Quality Review is conducted by banks.
Peer Review applies only to audit trainees, while Quality Review applies to retired members.
There is no difference; both are colloquial terms for income tax scrutiny.
questions.ref: Chartered Accountants Act, 1949 - Peer Review Board Statement & Section 28A Quality Review Board
questions.explanation: Peer Review is managed by ICAI's Peer Review Board to evaluate whether practice units have established adequate quality control policies (SQC 1) and complied with auditing standards. The Quality Review Board (QRB) is a statutory oversight body set up under Section 28A of the CA Act by the Central Government to evaluate quality of audit services in non-NFRA public interest entities.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Due Diligence and Special Purpose Audits
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Due Diligence - Target Working Capital & Peg Mechanism
questions.question: In an M&A share purchase transaction, what is the role of the 'Target Working Capital' (Working Capital Peg) established during due diligence?
options: It represents the mutually agreed normalized level of net working capital required to operate the business smoothly on closing date; any deficit on closing is deducted from purchase consideration, while surplus is added to purchase consideration.
It represents the maximum amount of cash that directors can withdraw as tax-free dividends.
It is a legal penalty paid to the stock exchange.
It is the minimum amount of bank borrowings the target must maintain.
questions.ref: ICAI Guidance Note on Due Diligence - Working Capital Peg and Closing Adjustments
questions.explanation: In M&A transactions, the Working Capital Peg is the baseline level of normalized net working capital expected to be delivered by the seller at completion. If actual closing working capital is less than the peg, the buyer pays less (downward price adjustment); if it exceeds the peg, the buyer pays an additional amount.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Due Diligence and Special Purpose Audits
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Investigation vs Audit
questions.question: Under auditing jurisprudence, which statement correctly summarizes the distinction between an 'Investigation' and an 'Audit'?
options: An audit is a general, periodic examination of financial statements to express an opinion on true and fair view with reasonable assurance; an investigation is a non-routine, in-depth inquiry conducted for a predetermined, specific purpose (e.g. suspected fraud, valuation, acquisition) without being constrained by conventional audit materiality.
An audit is criminal, while an investigation is purely mathematical.
An audit is done by lawyers, while an investigation is done by bank tellers.
Investigations are illegal in India without a warrant from the Supreme Court.
questions.ref: ICAI CA Final Study Material - Investigation vs Audit
questions.explanation: An audit is a statutory periodic review of accounts using test checks and sampling to express an opinion on truth and fairness with reasonable assurance. An investigation is a non-recurring examination for a specific purpose (fraud discovery, purchase of business, tax evasion) where the investigator digs deeply into facts without being restricted by general materiality thresholds.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Due Diligence and Special Purpose Audits
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Special Audit - Section 66 of CGST Act (GST Special Audit)
questions.question: Under Section 66 of the Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) Act, 2017, when can a GST Assistant Commissioner direct a registered taxable person to undergo Special Audit by a nominated Chartered Accountant or Cost Accountant?
options: If at any stage of scrutiny, inquiry, or investigation, the officer (with prior approval of Commissioner) is of opinion that value has not been correctly declared or credit availed is not within normal limits, the officer can direct special audit within 90 days (extendable by 90 days).
Whenever the taxpayer changes their registered office address.
Whenever the taxpayer's turnover exceeds ₹100 Crores automatically.
Special audit under GST was abolished in 2019.
questions.ref: Section 66 of CGST Act, 2017 - Special Audit by CA/CMA
questions.explanation: Under Section 66(1) of the CGST Act, if at any stage of scrutiny, inquiry, investigation, or any other proceedings, any officer not below the rank of Assistant Commissioner, having regard to nature and complexity of the case and interest of revenue, is of opinion that value has not been correctly declared or credit availed is not within normal limits, he may, with prior approval of Commissioner, direct a special audit by a nominated CA/CMA.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Due Diligence and Special Purpose Audits
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Due Diligence - Types of Due Diligence
questions.question: In a cross-border acquisition of an industrial manufacturer, which distinct due diligence workstreams are typically conducted alongside Financial Due Diligence?
options: Legal Due Diligence, Tax Due Diligence, Commercial/Market Due Diligence, Technical/Operational Due Diligence, Human Resources Due Diligence, and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Due Diligence.
Astrological Due Diligence and Feng Shui Due Diligence.
Social Media Influencer Due Diligence.
Municipal Garbage Due Diligence.
questions.ref: ICAI Guidance Note on Due Diligence - Comprehensive Types of Due Diligence
questions.explanation: A holistic M&A review comprises multiple specialized workstreams: (1) Financial Due Diligence; (2) Tax Due Diligence (historical tax liabilities/NOLs); (3) Legal Due Diligence (contracts, litigation, IP); (4) Commercial Due Diligence (market share, customer retention); (5) Operational/Technical; (6) HR; and (7) Environmental & ESG Due Diligence.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Digital Auditing and Computer-Assisted Audit Techniques (CAATs)
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Rule 11(g) - Audit Trail and Edit Log Reporting
questions.question: Under Rule 11(g) of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014, what is the statutory auditor's reporting duty regarding the 'Audit Trail' feature in accounting software?
options: State whether the company has used accounting software for maintaining books of account which has a feature of recording audit trail (edit log) facility, operating throughout the year for all transactions, ensuring the audit trail has not been tampered with, and that the audit trail has been preserved as per statutory requirements for record retention (8 years).
Verify whether the accounting software was purchased from a government software vendor.
Check whether company laptops are equipped with anti-virus software.
Audit trail reporting is voluntary and only applies to listed entities.
questions.ref: Rule 11(g) of Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014 & ICAI Implementation Guide on Audit Trail
questions.explanation: Under Rule 11(g), the auditor must report whether the company has used accounting software which has a feature of recording audit trail (edit log) facility, and the same has operated throughout the year for all transactions recorded in the software, and the audit trail feature has not been tampered with, and the audit trail has been preserved as per statutory requirements for record retention (Section 128(5) - 8 years).

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Digital Auditing and Computer-Assisted Audit Techniques (CAATs)
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] CAATs - Generalized Audit Software (GAS)
questions.question: What capabilities make Generalized Audit Software (GAS) (such as IDEA or ACL) a powerful tool for statutory and forensic auditors in testing large databases?
options: Ability to read diverse data formats without altering underlying client data, extract 100% of transactions matching specific criteria, perform duplicate checks, gap testing, stratified random sampling, join/merge disparate tables, and recalculate complex fields at high speed.
Ability to automatically write and publish the audit report without human intervention.
Ability to remotely control the client's bank accounts to freeze transactions.
Ability to generate fictitious invoices to balance debits and credits.
questions.ref: ICAI Guidance Note on Audit in Automated Environment - Generalized Audit Software
questions.explanation: Generalized Audit Software (GAS) provides independent data extraction and analysis capabilities. It allows auditors to import massive transactional datasets without data corruption, test 100% of populations, identify sequence gaps or duplicates, stratify samples, perform aging analysis, and verify computational accuracy independent of client IT controls.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Digital Auditing and Computer-Assisted Audit Techniques (CAATs)
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Automated Environment - IT General Controls (GITCs)
questions.question: In an automated ERP environment, what are the four core domains of Information Technology General Controls (ITGCs) evaluated by the digital auditor?
options: Access Security (user authentication, password policies, privilege management), Program Change Management, Data Center and Network Operations (backup and recovery), and Program Development / Acquisition.
Monitor display resolution, keyboard ergonomics, printer ink, and mouse speed.
Broadband speed, office lighting, air conditioning temperature, and cafeteria food.
Tax filing portals, MCA V3 system, GSTN server, and DigiLocker.
questions.ref: ICAI Implementation Guide on Auditing in an Automated Environment - ITGC Domains
questions.explanation: ITGCs encompass controls across four core domains: (1) Manage Access (user access, privileged access, segregation of duties); (2) Manage Changes (authorizing, testing, and migrating code changes); (3) Manage Operations (batch processing, data backups, disaster recovery); and (4) Program Development/Acquisition (system selection and implementation controls).

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Digital Auditing and Computer-Assisted Audit Techniques (CAATs)
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] CAATs - Test Data Technique
questions.question: How is the 'Test Data Technique' utilized by an auditor when testing automated application controls in an ERP system?
options: The auditor enters specially prepared dummy transactions (containing both valid and invalid test conditions) into the client's software to determine whether the automated controls correctly accept valid data and reject invalid data.
The auditor sends email questionnaires to all database administrators.
The auditor deletes the client's live production database to test server backups.
The auditor calculates depreciation manually with a pocket calculator.
questions.ref: ICAI CA Final Study Material - Computer-Assisted Audit Techniques (Test Data)
questions.explanation: Under the Test Data technique, the auditor prepares input data containing known valid and invalid data (e.g. negative prices, unauthorized customer codes, credit limit breaches) and processes it through the entity's computer program to check if controls operate as expected (e.g. error flags triggered, transactions rejected).

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Digital Auditing and Computer-Assisted Audit Techniques (CAATs)
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Automated Environment - Continuous Auditing & Embedded Audit Modules
questions.question: What is an 'Embedded Audit Module' (EAM) in continuous digital auditing?
options: Specially written audit code embedded directly within the client's host production software application that continuously monitors real-time transactional data and captures transactions meeting predetermined criteria (e.g. transfers exceeding ₹50 Lakhs) into a secure audit log for auditor review.
A physical hardware chip soldered onto the computer motherboard.
An anti-virus plugin that blocks incoming spam emails.
A software program that speeds up computer boot times.
questions.ref: ICAI Guidance Note on Audit in Automated Environment - Embedded Audit Modules (EAM)
questions.explanation: Embedded Audit Modules (EAMs) are segments of program code integrated directly into client application programs. They operate continuously in the background, intercepting transactions that meet specific risk parameters (e.g. unusual timing, high value, suspicious account combinations) and writing them to an auditor-controlled file (System Control Audit Review File - SCARF).

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Digital Auditing and Computer-Assisted Audit Techniques (CAATs)
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Rule 11(g) - Modification of Audit Report for Disabled Audit Trail
questions.question: During statutory audit for FY 2023-24, the auditor discovers that the client's accounting software had its audit trail feature turned off by the IT administrator for 45 days during the second quarter to 'speed up transaction processing'. How should the auditor report this under Rule 11(g)?
options: Issue a modified remark under the Rule 11(g) reporting section of the auditor's report, explicitly stating that the audit trail feature did not operate continuously throughout the year and specifying the period during which it was disabled.
Ignore the omission since it was disabled only for 45 days.
Issue an adverse opinion on the financial statements automatically.
Instruct management to back-date fake edit logs for the 45 days.
questions.ref: ICAI Implementation Guide on Reporting on Audit Trail under Rule 11(g)
questions.explanation: Under Rule 11(g) and the ICAI Implementation Guide, the audit trail facility must operate continuously throughout the year for all transactions recorded in the software. If the audit trail feature was disabled or not operating for any period during the year, the auditor must modify their report under Rule 11(g) stating the factual non-compliance.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Digital Auditing and Computer-Assisted Audit Techniques (CAATs)
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Digital Auditing - Cybersecurity Audit & Vulnerability Assessment
questions.question: In performing a cybersecurity audit of a fintech company's payment processing gateway, what is the purpose of Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT)?
options: Vulnerability assessment identifies and classifies security vulnerabilities in network and application components; penetration testing simulates real-world cyberattacks to evaluate whether vulnerabilities can be exploited to gain unauthorized access to financial data.
VAPT tests the typing speed of database operators.
VAPT checks whether office computers are cleaned of dust.
VAPT calculates employee payroll tax deductions.
questions.ref: RBI Cyber Security Framework & ICAI IT Audit Guidelines - VAPT
questions.explanation: Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT) is a core technical cybersecurity audit procedure. Vulnerability assessment is a non-intrusive scan to identify security weaknesses; penetration testing is an authorized simulated cyberattack to probe defenses, assess exploitability, and evaluate data leakage risks.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Digital Auditing and Computer-Assisted Audit Techniques (CAATs)
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Automated Environment - IT Dependent Manual Controls (ITDM)
questions.question: What is an 'IT-Dependent Manual Control' (ITDMC) in an enterprise risk framework?
options: A control that is performed manually by human intervention, but where the effectiveness of the control relies upon the completeness and accuracy of an automated IT-generated report or data (e.g. managerial review of an exception report produced by ERP).
A control performed exclusively by robotic arms on an assembly line.
A control that requires no computer systems whatsoever.
A manual signature on a paper cheque without checking bank balances.
questions.ref: ICAI Guidance Note on Internal Financial Controls - IT Dependent Manual Controls
questions.explanation: An IT-Dependent Manual Control is a hybrid control where a human performs a manual check (e.g. reviewing an aging analysis or margin report), but where the validity of the control depends entirely on the underlying automated system producing complete and accurate data (IPE - Information Produced by the Entity).

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Digital Auditing and Computer-Assisted Audit Techniques (CAATs)
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Digital Auditing - Data Analytics in Journal Entry Testing
questions.question: When applying data analytics to test journal entries under SA 240, which search parameters should the digital audit team query in the general ledger database to detect suspicious fraud entries?
options: Entries posted by unauthorized users, entries posted on weekends or public holidays, entries posted late at night (e.g. 11 PM to 4 AM), round sum amounts (e.g. exactly ₹50,00,000), entries with blank or vague narrations, entries posted just below approval thresholds, and entries debited to rarely used expense accounts.
Only entries ending in zero paise.
Only entries approved by the external auditor.
Entries that have already been audited in the previous year.
questions.ref: SA 240, Paragraph A43 & ICAI Data Analytics in Audit Guidelines
questions.explanation: Automated journal entry testing uses digital analytics to filter millions of transactions for high-risk characteristics: unauthorized user IDs, weekend/holiday postings, late-night timestamp clusters, round-number amounts, entries made immediately before or after reporting cutoff, entries debited to unusual account pairs, and entries with suppressed descriptions.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Corporate Governance and Quality Control
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SEBI (LODR) Regulation 18 - Audit Committee Constitution
questions.question: Under Regulation 18 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, what are the mandatory constitution requirements for the Audit Committee of a listed entity?
options: Minimum three directors as members, at least two-thirds of the members shall be independent directors, all members shall be financially literate, and at least one member shall have accounting or related financial management expertise, with an independent director as Chairperson.
Minimum two directors, both being executive whole-time directors.
Minimum five directors, all of whom must be government nominees.
The Managing Director must be the Chairperson of the Audit Committee.
questions.ref: SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 - Regulation 18(1) Constitution of Audit Committee
questions.explanation: Under Regulation 18(1) of SEBI (LODR): (a) The audit committee shall have minimum 3 directors as members; (b) At least two-thirds of the members shall be independent directors; (c) All members of audit committee shall be financially literate and at least one member shall have accounting or related financial management expertise; (d) The Chairperson shall be an independent director and present at AGM.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Corporate Governance and Quality Control
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SQC 1 - Six Elements of Quality Control System
questions.question: Under Standard on Quality Control (SQC) 1 'Quality Control for Firms that Perform Audits and Reviews of Historical Financial Information', which of the following lists the SIX essential elements of a firm's system of quality control?
options: Leadership Responsibilities for Quality within the Firm, Ethical Requirements, Acceptance and Continuance of Client Relationships and Specific Engagements, Human Resources, Engagement Performance, and Monitoring.
Marketing, Billing, Collection, Tax Planning, Litigation, and Arbitration.
Statutory Audit, Internal Audit, Forensic Audit, Tax Audit, GST Audit, and Stock Audit.
Managing Partner, Senior Partner, Junior Partner, Audit Manager, Article Trainee, and Office Peon.
questions.ref: SQC 1, Paragraph 6 - Elements of a System of Quality Control
questions.explanation: Under SQC 1.6, the firm's system of quality control must include policies and procedures addressing six elements: (1) Leadership responsibilities for quality within the firm; (2) Ethical requirements; (3) Acceptance and continuance of client relationships and specific engagements; (4) Human resources; (5) Engagement performance; and (6) Monitoring.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Corporate Governance and Quality Control
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SEBI (LODR) Regulation 18(2) - Audit Committee Quorum & Meetings
questions.question: Under Regulation 18(2) of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, how many times must the Audit Committee meet in a year, what is the maximum permissible gap between meetings, and what is the quorum?
options: The audit committee shall meet at least 4 times in a year and not more than 120 days shall elapse between two meetings; quorum shall be either 2 members or one-third of the members (whichever is greater), with at least 2 independent directors present.
Meet at least 12 times a year (monthly) with quorum of 5 independent directors.
Meet once every 2 years with no quorum requirement.
Meet only when summoned by the stock exchange.
questions.ref: SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 - Regulation 18(2) Meetings and Quorum of Audit Committee
questions.explanation: Under Regulation 18(2) of SEBI (LODR): (a) The audit committee shall meet at least four times in a year and not more than 120 days shall elapse between two meetings; (b) The quorum for audit committee meeting shall either be two members or one-third of the members of the audit committee, whichever is greater, with at least two independent directors.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Corporate Governance and Quality Control
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Section 132 - Penal Powers of NFRA for Professional Misconduct
questions.question: Under Section 132(4)(c) of the Companies Act, 2013, what penalties can the National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA) impose on an individual auditor or an audit firm if professional or other misconduct is proved?
options: For an individual: fine of not less than ₹1 Lakh (extendable to 5 times fees); For a firm: fine of not less than ₹5 Lakhs (extendable to 10 times fees); AND debarring the member/firm from engaging in audit practice for a minimum period of 6 months up to a maximum period of 10 years.
Strictly a written reprimand with zero monetary penalty.
Suspension of the auditor's passport for 50 years.
NFRA has no power to impose penalties; it can only write letters to ICAI.
questions.ref: Section 132(4)(c) of Companies Act, 2013 - Penal Powers of NFRA
questions.explanation: Under Section 132(4)(c), where professional or other misconduct is proved, NFRA has the power to make order imposing penalty: (i) Not less than ₹1 Lakh which may extend to 5 times the fees received in case of individuals; (ii) Not less than ₹5 Lakhs which may extend to 10 times fees in case of firms; and (B) Debarring the member or firm from being appointed as an auditor for a minimum of 6 months up to 10 years.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Corporate Governance and Quality Control
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Section 177 - Audit Committee Mandatory Review of Information
questions.question: Under Section 177 of the Companies Act, 2013 and SEBI (LODR) Part C of Schedule II, which of the following is MANDATORILY reviewed by the Audit Committee?
options: Management Discussion and Analysis (MD&A), statement of significant related party transactions, management letters/letters of internal control weaknesses issued by statutory auditors, internal audit reports relating to internal control weaknesses, appointment/removal/remuneration of Chief Internal Auditor, and statement of deviations in use of IPO/rights issue proceeds.
Personal leave records and holiday plans of marketing executives.
Canteen food menu and office decoration invoices.
Political donations made by individual shareholders in their personal capacities.
questions.ref: SEBI (LODR) Schedule II, Part C & Section 177 of Companies Act, 2013 - Mandatory Review by Audit Committee
questions.explanation: Under SEBI (LODR) Schedule II, Part C, the Audit Committee must mandatorily review: (1) MD&A of financial condition; (2) Statement of significant related party transactions; (3) Management letters issued by statutory auditors; (4) Internal audit reports relating to internal control weaknesses; (5) Appointment, removal, and remuneration of Chief Internal Auditor; and (6) Statement of deviations under Reg 32.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Corporate Governance and Quality Control
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SQC 1 - Engagement Quality Control Review (EQCR) Criteria
questions.question: Under SQC 1 and SA 220, for which types of engagements is an Engagement Quality Control Review (EQCR) MANDATORY prior to the issuance of the audit report?
options: Mandatory for all audits of financial statements of listed entities, and for those other audit engagements meeting criteria established by the firm (e.g. public interest entities, high-risk or unusual regulatory profile).
Only for small proprietary businesses.
Only if requested by the local income tax assessing officer.
EQCR is optional and never mandatory for any firm.
questions.ref: SQC 1, Paragraph 60 & SA 220, Paragraph 19 - Mandatory EQCR for Listed Entities
questions.explanation: SQC 1.60 and SA 220 mandate that the firm shall establish policies and procedures requiring, for appropriate engagements, an engagement quality control review. Such review is explicitly mandatory for all audits of financial statements of listed entities. For other engagements, the firm establishes objective criteria based on risk, public interest, and regulatory scrutiny.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Corporate Governance and Quality Control
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SEBI (LODR) Regulation 17 - Board Composition & Independent Directors
questions.question: Under Regulation 17(1) of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, if the Chairperson of the Board of Directors of a listed entity is a Non-Executive Director who is a PROMOTER or related to a promoter, what minimum proportion of the Board must consist of Independent Directors?
options: At least half (50%) of the Board of Directors shall consist of independent directors.
At least one-third (33.33%) of the Board.
Only one independent director is required.
Independent directors are not permitted on the board.
questions.ref: SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 - Regulation 17(1)(b) Board Composition
questions.explanation: Under Regulation 17(1)(b) of SEBI (LODR), where the chairperson of the board of directors is a non-executive director, at least one-third of the board shall comprise independent directors. However, where the regular non-executive chairperson is a promoter of the listed entity or is related to any promoter or person occupying high management positions, at least half (50%) of the board shall consist of independent directors.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Corporate Governance and Quality Control
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SQC 1 - Differences of Opinion Resolution
questions.question: Under SQC 1, when differences of opinion arise within the engagement team, with those consulted, or between the engagement partner and the engagement quality control reviewer, what policy must the firm follow before issuing the audit report?
options: The firm's policies must ensure that differences of opinion are resolved through documented consultation/mediation, conclusions reached are documented and implemented, and the report is NOT released until the matter is resolved.
The engagement partner can unilaterally override all objections and release the report immediately without documentation.
The firm must refer the dispute to the local police station.
The youngest article trainee's vote decides the dispute.
questions.ref: SQC 1, Paragraphs 56-59 - Differences of Opinion in Quality Control
questions.explanation: Under SQC 1.56-59, the firm shall establish policies and procedures for dealing with and resolving differences of opinion within the engagement team, with those consulted and between the engagement partner and the engagement quality control reviewer. Such policies shall require that conclusions reached be documented and implemented, and the report shall not be issued until the difference of opinion is resolved.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Corporate Governance and Quality Control
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SEBI (LODR) Regulation 27 - Corporate Governance Quarterly Compliance
questions.question: Under Regulation 27(2) of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, what is the mandatory quarterly compliance filing deadline for listed entities regarding Corporate Governance?
options: Submit a quarterly compliance report on corporate governance in the format specified by the Board to the recognized stock exchange(s) within 21 days from the end of each quarter.
Within 90 days of the Annual General Meeting.
Annually within 6 months of fiscal year-end.
Filing is required only once every 5 years.
questions.ref: SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 - Regulation 27(2) Quarterly Corporate Governance Report
questions.explanation: Under Regulation 27(2)(a) of SEBI (LODR), the listed entity shall submit a quarterly compliance report on corporate governance in the format specified by SEBI to the recognized stock exchange(s) within 21 days from the end of each quarter. The report details board composition, committee meetings, and related party transactions.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Code of Ethics and Professional Misconduct Under the Chartered Accountants Act
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] First Schedule, Part I, Clause 6 - Solicitation of Professional Work
questions.question: CA Vikram issued a circular letter to 500 manufacturing companies across Gujarat who were not his existing clients, describing the specialized tax advisory capabilities of his firm and inviting them to appoint his firm for GST litigation. Under the First Schedule to the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949, is CA Vikram guilty of professional misconduct?
options: Yes, guilty under Clause (6) of Part I of the First Schedule for soliciting client or professional work either directly or indirectly by circular, advertisement, personal communication, or interview, or by any other means.
No, because Chartered Accountants have a fundamental right under the Constitution to advertise commercial services.
No, provided Vikram did not mention his professional fees in the circular.
Only if another Chartered Accountant files an injunction in the High Court.
questions.ref: First Schedule to the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949 - Part I, Clause (6)
questions.explanation: Under Clause (6) of Part I of the First Schedule, a Chartered Accountant in practice is deemed to be guilty of professional misconduct if he solicits clients or professional work either directly or indirectly by circular, advertisement, personal communication or interview or by any other means. Sending circulars to non-clients directly violates Clause 6.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Code of Ethics and Professional Misconduct Under the Chartered Accountants Act
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] First Schedule, Part I, Clause 8 - Prior Communication with Previous Auditor
questions.question: CA Neha accepts appointment as statutory auditor of Zenith Steels Ltd. without first communicating in writing with the retiring previous auditor, CA Prakash. She states that since the company's AGM passed a valid resolution appointing her and ROC filings were completed, prior communication with the retiring auditor was a mere formality. Is Neha guilty of professional misconduct?
options: Yes, guilty under Clause (8) of Part I of the First Schedule for accepting a position as auditor previously held by another chartered accountant without first communicating with him in writing.
No, because the shareholder resolution in AGM is supreme over professional bylaws.
No, provided Neha sends an email 3 months after accepting the audit.
No, because prior communication is voluntary under the New Scheme of ICAI.
questions.ref: First Schedule to the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949 - Part I, Clause (8)
questions.explanation: Under Clause (8) of Part I of the First Schedule, a CA in practice is deemed guilty of professional misconduct if he accepts a position as auditor previously held by another chartered accountant without first communicating with him in writing. Such communication must be in writing (via registered post with acknowledgement due, speed post, or verifiable digital means) prior to acceptance.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Code of Ethics and Professional Misconduct Under the Chartered Accountants Act
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Revised Code of Ethics - NOCLAR (Non-Compliance with Laws & Regulations)
questions.question: Under the Revised ICAI Code of Ethics (2020), what is the scope and mandatory applicability of NOCLAR (Responding to Non-Compliance with Laws and Regulations)?
options: Applies to audit engagements of listed entities for senior professional accountants in practice; requires the professional accountant who encounters or becomes aware of non-compliance or suspected non-compliance with laws affecting financial statements or operating integrity to understand the matter, address it with management/TCWG, and determine whether disclosure to appropriate public authorities is required in the public interest.
Applies only to criminal defamation cases.
Requires all CAs to disclose every client transaction to the local police weekly.
NOCLAR is purely voluntary and has zero ethical standing in India.
questions.ref: ICAI Revised Code of Ethics (2020) - Section 260 & Section 360 (NOCLAR)
questions.explanation: NOCLAR sets out the framework for professional accountants when encountering illegal acts or suspected non-compliance. In India, it currently applies to audits of listed entities. When serious non-compliance (fraud, corruption, money laundering, environmental crime) is identified, the auditor must engage management/TCWG, and if they fail to take appropriate rectifying steps, evaluate whether overriding client confidentiality to disclose to regulatory authorities is required in the public interest.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Code of Ethics and Professional Misconduct Under the Chartered Accountants Act
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Second Schedule, Part I, Clause 7 - Gross Negligence in Professional Duties
questions.question: CA Rohan audited the financial statements of a finance company having assets of ₹400 Crores. He signed an unmodified audit report without verifying the existence of cash balances of ₹85 Crores or checking whether loan securities were registered with ROC. The company subsequently collapsed due to non-existent cash and unbacked loans. Under which provision is CA Rohan liable?
options: Guilty under Clause (7) of Part I of the Second Schedule for being grossly negligent in the conduct of his professional duties.
Guilty under Clause (1) of Part I of the First Schedule for sharing fees with an advocate.
Guilty under Clause (2) of Part II of the First Schedule for failing to pay Council fees.
Rohan is not liable because the auditor is a watchdog, not a bloodhound.
questions.ref: Second Schedule to the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949 - Part I, Clause (7)
questions.explanation: Under Clause (7) of Part I of the Second Schedule, a member in practice is deemed to be guilty of professional misconduct if he does not exercise due diligence, or is grossly negligent in the conduct of his professional duties. Failing to perform fundamental verification of 21% of total balance sheet assets (cash and securities) constitutes gross professional negligence.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Code of Ethics and Professional Misconduct Under the Chartered Accountants Act
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] First Schedule, Part I, Clause 10 - Contingent Fees & Percentage of Profits
questions.question: CA Arvind agrees to represent a corporate client before the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) on the terms that his professional fee will be calculated strictly as '15% of the total tax demand deleted by the Tribunal'. Under the Chartered Accountants Act, is CA Arvind guilty of professional misconduct?
options: Yes, guilty under Clause (10) of Part I of the First Schedule for charging or accepting fees which are based on a percentage of profits or which are contingent upon the findings or results of such employment (unless permitted under Regulation 192, which does not exempt tax litigation percentage fees).
No, because charging contingent fees for court representation is standard commercial practice.
No, provided the agreement is executed on judicial stamp paper.
Only if the tax demand deleted exceeds ₹10 Crores.
questions.ref: First Schedule to the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949 - Part I, Clause (10) & Regulation 192
questions.explanation: Under Clause (10) of Part I of the First Schedule, a member in practice is guilty of misconduct if he charges or accepts fees which are based on a percentage of profits or contingent upon findings. While Regulation 192 provides narrow exceptions (e.g. liquidator fees, debt recovery percentage for non-audit clients, valuer fees in certain cases), charging a percentage of tax relief deleted in litigation is strictly prohibited.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Code of Ethics and Professional Misconduct Under the Chartered Accountants Act
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Revised Code of Ethics - Fee Dependence on Public Interest Entities (>15%)
questions.question: Under Section 410 of the Revised ICAI Code of Ethics (2020), what mandatory safeguard must an audit firm implement if the gross fees received from a single Public Interest Entity (PIE) audit client exceed 15% of the firm's total gross fee revenue for two consecutive years?
options: The firm must disclose the fee dependence to TCWG and arrange for an Engagement Quality Review by an external professional accountant (either pre-issuance EQR before opinion is signed, or post-issuance review); if fee dependence continues beyond 5 consecutive years, the firm CANNOT continue as auditor.
The firm must refund the excess fee above 15% to the Central Government.
The firm must immediately surrender its ICAI firm registration.
No safeguards are required because fee dependence only applies at 50%.
questions.ref: ICAI Revised Code of Ethics (2020) - Section 410: Fees and Public Interest Entity Dependence
questions.explanation: Under Section 410 of the revised Code of Ethics, where fees from a Public Interest Entity (PIE) exceed 15% of the firm's total fees for two consecutive years, the firm must disclose this to TCWG and apply safeguards: pre-issuance review by external accountant or post-issuance review. If dependence continues for 5 consecutive years, the firm must cease acting as auditor.

questions.subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
questions.topicTitle: Code of Ethics and Professional Misconduct Under the Chartered Accountants Act
questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] First Schedule, Part I, Clause 11 - Engaging in Other Business or Occupation
questions.question: CA Gaurav, holding a full-time Certificate of Practice (COP), starts a partnership business with his brother to run a restaurant and acts as a working partner drawing monthly salary and profit share without obtaining prior permission of the Council of ICAI. Under which clause is CA Gaurav guilty of professional misconduct?
options: Guilty under Clause (11) of Part I of the First Schedule for engaging in any business or occupation other than the profession of chartered accountants unless permitted by the Council.
Guilty under Clause (2) of Part I of the Second Schedule for certifying accounts in which he has substantial interest.
Guilty under Clause (5) of Part I of the First Schedule for securing business through unauthorized means.
Gaurav is not guilty because food businesses are exempt under Council general guidelines.
questions.ref: First Schedule to the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949 - Part I, Clause (11) & Regulation 190A
questions.explanation: Under Clause (11) of Part I of the First Schedule, a CA in practice is guilty of misconduct if he engages in any business or occupation other than the profession of chartered accountancy unless permitted by the Council. While Regulation 190A grants general permission for certain activities (e.g. authorship of books, teaching up to specified hours, sleeping partner in family firm), acting as an active working partner in a commercial restaurant requires specific prior permission of Council.

questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Second Schedule, Part I, Clause 4 - Substantial Interest in Client Entity
questions.question: CA Deepa is the statutory auditor of Surya Power Ltd. Her husband holds 22% of the paid-up equity share capital of Surya Power Ltd. Deepa signs the statutory audit report certifying the financial statements as presenting a true and fair view. Under which provision is CA Deepa guilty of professional misconduct?
options: Guilty under Clause (4) of Part I of the Second Schedule for expressing an opinion on financial statements of an enterprise in which she, her firm, or a partner in her firm has a substantial interest.
Guilty under Clause (1) of Part I of the First Schedule.
Guilty under Clause (3) of Part II of the Second Schedule.
Deepa is not guilty because her husband's shareholding cannot affect her professional independence.
questions.ref: Second Schedule to the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949 - Part I, Clause (4) & Council Guidelines
questions.explanation: Under Clause (4) of Part I of the Second Schedule, a member in practice is guilty of misconduct if he expresses an opinion on financial statements of any business or enterprise in which he, his firm, or a partner in his firm has a substantial interest. Under Council guidelines, 'substantial interest' includes interest held by relatives (spouse, parents, siblings, children). 22% voting power held by husband constitutes substantial interest.

questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Second Schedule, Part I, Clause 8 - Failure to Obtain Sufficient Audit Evidence
questions.question: Under Clause (8) of Part I of the Second Schedule to the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949, when is a member in practice deemed to be guilty of professional misconduct regarding audit evidence?
options: If he fails to obtain sufficient information which is necessary for expression of an opinion or its exceptions are sufficiently material to negate the expression of an opinion.
If he asks more than 10 questions to the CFO.
If he fails to retain audit documentation for 50 years.
If he charges audit fees below the ICAI recommended minimum scale.
questions.ref: Second Schedule to the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949 - Part I, Clause (8)
questions.explanation: Under Clause (8) of Part I of the Second Schedule, a member in practice is deemed to be guilty of professional misconduct if he fails to obtain sufficient information which is necessary for expression of an opinion or its exceptions are sufficiently material to negate the expression of an opinion. Expressing a clean opinion without obtaining SAAE breaches Clause 8.

questions.tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] First Schedule, Part I, Clause 7 - Designations and Self-Praise on Letterheads
questions.question: CA Manas prints his visiting cards and stationery using the designation: 'CA Manas, Income Tax Specialist, Mergers & Corporate Restructuring Guru, Gold Medallist'. Under the First Schedule to the Chartered Accountants Act, is CA Manas guilty of professional misconduct?
options: Yes, guilty under Clause (7) of Part I of the First Schedule for using any designation or description other than Chartered Accountant on professional documents, visiting cards, letterheads, or signboards, and for advertising professional attainments.
No, because mentioning true university medals and professional specializations is encouraged.
No, provided Manas does not print his mobile phone number.
Only if the letterhead is printed in red ink.
questions.ref: First Schedule to the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949 - Part I, Clause (7) & Section 7 of the Act
questions.explanation: Under Clause (7) of Part I of the First Schedule read with Section 7 of the CA Act, a member in practice is prohibited from using any designation or description other than that of 'Chartered Accountant' on professional documents, letterheads, or visiting cards. Using self-laudatory descriptions like 'Specialist' or 'Guru' directly breaches Clause 7.
